cues.en: Suddenly, these rogue ants no longer serve the colony. They're taking their orders from the parasite. Okay, let's back up. Now, how did this happen? It all begins when the ants in any town USA consume the slime of a passing snail. They divide it up and take it back to the colony. This is a blunder of epic proportions. Turns out...
cues.zh: 突然间，这些行为反常的蚂蚁不再为蚁群服务了。它们开始听命于寄生虫。好吧，让我们倒回去看看。这到底是怎么发生的呢？一切始于美国某处小镇的蚂蚁吞食了一只路过蜗牛的黏液。它们分食黏液，并带回了蚁群。这是一个极其致命的错误。事实证明……

cues.en: The slime is loaded with eggs of a body snatcher called the liver fluke, a type of flatworm. The liver fluke burrows into a part of the ant's brain, and for unknown reasons, it's almost like the fluke enslaves the ants and orders them to carry it to their next hosts. Any grazing mammal host with a nice warm liver will do, but in this case a cow appears.
cues.zh: 黏液里充满了掠夺者“肝吸虫”的卵，这是一种扁形虫。肝吸虫钻进蚂蚁大脑的某个部位，出于未知的原因，这种吸虫就像奴役了蚂蚁一样，命令它们将自己带到下一个宿主那里。任何拥有温暖肝脏的草食性哺乳动物宿主都行，不过这一次，一头牛出现了。

cues.en: The liver fluke worms can switch the ants' behavior on and off, causing the infected ants to place themselves in easy-to-eat positions at dusk when mammals are feeding. No cows in sight, ants act normal. Cows appear, ants are in essence ordered to take their positions in purple flowers and latch on. The cows ingest the vegetation, the ants, and the fluke larvae inside the ants all in one bite.
cues.zh: 肝吸虫可以随意操控蚂蚁的行为，促使受感染的蚂蚁在黄昏哺乳动物进食时，把自己置于极易被吃掉的位置。看不到牛时，蚂蚁表现正常。牛一出现，蚂蚁就基本上被命令爬上紫色花朵就位并紧紧咬住。牛把植被、蚂蚁，连同蚂蚁体内的吸虫幼虫一口吞下。

cues.en: Once inside the cow, the worms burrow out of the stomach and into the liver, where they develop into adults and dine on liver tissue. They lay eggs that are excreted from the liver into the bile duct, and then defecated by the cows. They don't kill the cows, but the cows become weak and emaciated, devastating herds. And all because of parasitic mind controlling.
cues.zh: 一旦进入牛的体内，这些虫子就会钻出胃部进入肝脏，在那里发育为成虫并以肝组织为食。它们产下的卵会从肝脏排入胆管，然后随牛粪排出体外。它们不会致牛死亡，但牛会变得虚弱消瘦，对牛群造成严重打击。而这一切，都源于寄生虫的精神控制。

cues.en: I have the good fortune to be both a game designer and a programmer. And that's pretty cool, because what I do from day to day in my working life is I decide what to do, and then I just type it in and make it work somehow on a computer. This is different from what a lot of people in games do, where they have to get an idea and get permission to implement that idea, or else they have to do someone else's idea that they think is kind of stupid. Because of this, I have a lot of freedom in terms of what I work on and what I've been doing.
cues.zh: 我很庆幸自己既是一名游戏设计师，又是一名程序员。这感觉很棒，因为在日常工作中，我想做什么就决定做什么，然后直接敲代码把它在电脑上跑起来。这与许多游戏从业者不同，他们得先有个点子，然后获得批准才能去实现，否则就只能去执行别人那些在他们看来有点蠢的想法。正因如此，我在做什么工作方面拥有很大的自由度，而我一直在做的……

cues.en: for the past several years, at least, is figuring out ways to make games that I think are deeper than current video games or more meaningful than a lot of video games. But those kind of phrases, like deeper, tend to set people on edge. They're like, oh, what's wrong with current video games? You're saying current video games aren't good. They're not deep. And so there's a phrase that I've sort of learned to adopt a little bit that helps
cues.zh: ……至少在过去的几年里，一直在探索如何制作我认为比现今电子游戏更深刻、或比许多电子游戏更有意义的游戏。但像“更深刻”这样的字眼往往容易让人反感。人们会觉得：“哦，现在的电子游戏怎么了？你是说现在的电子游戏不好？不够深刻吗？”因此，我学会了采用一种表达方式，它有助于……

cues.en: discussions proceed without being argumentative, right? And it's this phrase, speaking to the human condition, right? This is a traditional thing that we say about art, right? When people talk about the good parts of films and novels and paintings and music and sculpture, and they talk about how these things can affect people deeply or change their lives or reveal truths to them, we'll say that these works speak to the human condition.
cues.zh: ……在不引发争论的情况下推进讨论，对吧？这个表达就是：“触及人类的生存境况”，对吧？这是我们评价艺术时的传统说法，对吧？当人们谈论电影、小说、绘画、音乐和雕塑的优秀之处时，当他们谈论这些艺术品如何能深深打动人心、改变人们的生活或向他们揭示真理时，我们就会说，这些作品触及了人类的生存境况。

cues.en: But the magic of this phrase is that it's pretty vague, right? Nobody will agree or even nobody knows exactly what it means. But that's actually part of what allows us to employ it usefully, right, to have discussions. It's a little bit of a paradox there. But I and many other game designers who are sort of in my school of thought, not my school of thought, but in a common school of thought,
cues.zh: 这个说法的魔力在于它很模糊，对吧？没人会达成一致，甚至没人确切知道它是什么意思。但这其实正是我们能有效使用它、展开讨论的部分原因。这里面有点悖论。但我以及许多其他游戏设计师，算是和我同一思想流派，不，不是我的流派，而是共同的思想流派，

cues.en: We feel like games so far don't do a very good job of speaking to the human condition, whatever that means for each individual person, each individual designer. And so we're working on that. We feel like games currently tend to be temporary diversions, something I do for a little bit, but I don't really care about in the same level of magnitude as the things that are truly important in my life. And so the operative question for me is, can that ever be changed? Can games become a medium deeply important to people?
cues.zh: 我们觉得到目前为止，游戏在触及人类境况方面做得并不好——不管这对每个人、每个设计师各自意味着什么。所以我们正在努力。我们觉得现在的游戏往往只是临时消遣，是我会玩一会儿、但不会像生活中真正重要的事情那样在意的东西。所以对我来说，关键问题是：这有可能改变吗？游戏能成为一种对人们至关重要的媒介吗？

cues.en: deeply important to more people than a professional StarCraft player or something like that. So let me set some context for this discussion. I'm going to talk about a couple of really old games from the 1980s. This first game is Pac-Man. I think even today, everybody knows this game. It's an arcade game. It's very simple. You run around this maze, and you collect dots, and you try not to get killed by the ghosts, except sometimes you can turn around and eat the ghosts.
cues.zh: 对更多人来说都至关重要，而不只是对职业 StarCraft 玩家之类的人重要。让我先为这个讨论提供一些背景。我要谈几款1980年代非常老的游戏。第一款是 Pac-Man。我觉得即使今天，大家也都知道这个游戏。它是街机游戏，非常简单。你在迷宫里跑来跑去，收集豆子，尽量别被幽灵杀死，不过有时候你也可以转身吃掉幽灵。

cues.en: It's a fun game. Even today, it's kind of fun to play. It had good game feel for the time, which is just the way the controls feel and the way the sound effects sync with the graphics and stuff. But most people I know would not say that Pac-Man really speaks to the human condition. This is not going to be a game that you go, oh, it changed my life. It was really meaningful to me. No, it's a fun game. But it's just about running around a maze eating dots.
cues.zh: 它是个好玩的游戏。即使今天，玩起来也还挺有趣。它在当时有很好的游戏手感，也就是操控的感觉，以及音效与画面等同步的方式。但我认识的大多数人不会说 Pac-Man 真的触及了人类境况。这不会是你玩完后会说“哦，它改变了我的人生，它对我意义重大”的那种游戏。不，它就是个好玩的游戏。无非是在迷宫里跑来跑去吃豆子。

cues.en: Simple, simple game. Here's another game. Most people probably don't know what this is. Does anyone know what this game is without reading the caption? No. It's a game called Impossible Mission. The first platform it was released for was a Commodore 64. And it's a James Bond kind of game where you're infiltrating an evil genius's underground fortress to stop a nuclear launch or something like that. This was pretty much the halo of 1984 or something like that.
cues.zh: 很简单，很简单的游戏。这是另一款游戏。大多数人可能不知道这是什么。有人不读说明文字就知道这是什么游戏吗？没有。它叫 Impossible Mission。最早发行的平台是 Commodore 64。它是那种 James Bond 式的游戏：你潜入一个邪恶天才的地下堡垒，阻止核发射之类的。这差不多就是1984年的 Halo 之类的。

cues.en: In addition to being very ugly, though, by modern standards, it's also kind of unplayable by modern standards. You kind of take these elevators around, and you're trying to reach these obstacles on the level so you can search them and find things. And you're trying to jump over these robots that shoot lightning out. And so it's all this pixel perfect jumping and not falling into the gap and things like that, which video games of today still use once in a while.
cues.zh: 不过，除了以现代标准看非常丑之外，它按现代标准也有点没法玩。你乘这些电梯到处走，试图到达关卡里的这些障碍点，好搜索它们并找到东西。你还要跳过那些会射出闪电的机器人。所以全是那种像素级精准跳跃、不能掉进缝隙之类的操作，今天的电子游戏偶尔还会用。

cues.en: This game is like 100% pixel perfect jumping and you get fried and you have to restart at the save point and do all this hard stuff over again. It's all these things that since then us video game designers have learned not to do because when you make things really difficult, when you throw a bunch of challenge at the player but they can see that the thing you're challenging them with is relatively meaningless like jumping over these stupid robots, then they tend to just stop caring about it very quickly, right? Now the reason people love this game back then is because this was new.
cues.zh: 这款游戏全靠像素级的精准跳跃，一旦被电死就得在存档点复活，把那些折磨人的难关重打一遍。从那之后，我们游戏设计师就学会了别这么做，因为一旦你把游戏做得极难、堆一堆挑战给玩家，而他们又发现这些挑战本身毫无意义——比如跳过这些愚蠢的机器人——他们很快就会直接弃坑，对吧？当年人们之所以喜欢这款游戏，是因为它很新鲜。

cues.en: wow, I'd never played a game where I can pretend I'm James Bond and infiltrate this mountain fortress. But now we've played so many, I would say, better video games that nobody wants to go back and play this. So in the couple of decades since then, game designers as a community have learned some best practices to help them make games that are either more playable and more enjoyable by a wider audience than something like Impossible Mission.
cues.zh: 哇，我以前从没玩过能假装自己是 James Bond、潜入这座山中要塞的游戏。但现在我们玩过太多可以说是更好的游戏了，以至于没人会想回去玩这个。所以在之后的几十年里，整个游戏设计圈总结出了一些最佳实践，来帮助制作更耐玩、比《不可能的任务》（Impossible Mission）能吸引更广泛受众的游戏。

cues.en: Or things that are larger and more intricate and deeper than Pac-Man, right? And if I were to write out the full list of what game designers have figured out, it would be many, many pages. I mean, I could probably write books on it, not that I would ever want to. But I've sort of picked four of the major things that all of you guys are going to recognize, assuming you've ever played a video game. The first thing that we learned to do is put
cues.zh: 或者是比 Pac-Man 更庞大、更错综复杂、更深度的游戏，对吧？如果要把游戏设计师们摸索出的心得全写下来，那得有好几十页。我的意思是，我可能都能为此写上几本书了，虽然我压根不想写。但我挑出了四个主要的点，只要你们玩过电子游戏，肯定都能感同身受。我们学到的第一件事就是：

cues.en: story in a game in a very concrete, progressing way. The story of impossible mission is like, hey, you're a secret agent, and you're trying to infiltrate this fortress, but that story doesn't progress. There's no plot points or anything. It's just you're trying to do this, and then you eventually solve enough puzzles and win the game. Humans like to hear stories.
cues.zh: 在游戏中以一种非常具体、步步推进的方式讲述故事。《不可能的任务》的故事差不多就是：“嘿，你是个特工，你想潜入这座要塞”，但故事并不会推进。没有任何剧情转折点之类的东西。仅仅是你要去做这件事，最后解开足够的谜题通关游戏。人都是喜欢听故事的。

cues.en: You know, stories have a magnetism. We want to know what happens next. And what game designers have learned to do is take that desire to find out what happens next and help use it kind of as a rope to pull you along through a video game. Now, in addition to pulling you through the game, it has a secondary function, which is to justify what you're doing with a fictional excuse. If you play old school
cues.zh: 故事有一种吸引力。我们都想知道接下来会发生什么。游戏设计师学到的，就是利用玩家“想知道后续”的欲望，像绳子一样拉着你一路通关。除了引导你通关之外，它还有第二个作用：给玩家的行为找一个剧情上的合理借口。如果你玩过老派的

cues.en: first-person shooters like Doom or games like that really literally at the dawn of the first-person shooter the way it would work is you're running around shooting a bunch of monsters and you're trying to get to the end of the level and you run into a door and it's a red door and you know that to get to the red door you need to find the red card key right and so you go find that and you go open the door and you keep going and eventually there's a blue door and you know you need to find the blue card key right and that was literally the way these games were paced for a while after that is just there's these
cues.zh: 第一人称射击游戏，比如 Doom 或者第一人称射击游戏刚诞生时的那些作品，它们的套路就是：你到处跑动射杀一群怪物，努力通关到关底，然后遇到一扇门，是一扇红门，你就知道要开红门就得去找红色钥匙卡，对吧？于是你找到钥匙开门继续走，接着又遇到一扇蓝门，你就知道得找蓝色钥匙卡，对吧？在那之后有段时间，这些游戏的节奏基本全都是这样，仅仅是用一些

cues.en: relatively arbitrary game mechanical things preventing you from progressing. Now there's a green door, right? And you knew exactly what you had to do to get through the door, but there's no reason for it, right? Now we have games like, you know, Modern Warfare where it's like, oh, we need to drive this tank to the next mission, but the tank's out of gas and the guys are like infiltrating the fuel depot, so you need to like shoot a bunch of them and get in there and get some gas cans and bring it back to the tank and fill up the tank so our boys can drive on to the next mission.
cues.zh: 相对随意的游戏机制来阻碍你的推进。现在又来了一扇绿门，对吧？你非常清楚要开门该做什么，但这毫无情理可言，对吧？而现在的游戏，比如大家熟知的 Modern Warfare，剧情就会变成：“我们需要开着这辆坦克去执行下一个任务，但坦克没油了，敌人正在潜入油库，所以你得干掉他们，潜入油库搞几个油桶带回坦克这里加满油，这样我们的弟兄们才能继续开拔去执行下一个任务。”

cues.en: It's really the same thing as the red key and the red door, but now there's like this huge scaffolding around it to make it fictionally plausible and to try to make it engrossing, right? Another thing we've learned to do is add a bunch of eye candy and ear candy like nice sound effects to games because human beings like visual and oral stimulation, aural stimulation. And, you know, often the more of that the better, even if it's subtle, even if you're looking at a game that's
cues.zh: 这其实和“红钥匙配红门”是一回事，只是现在外面搭了巨大的脚手架，让它在虚构设定里显得合理，也尽量让人沉浸，对吧？我们还学会的另一件事，是给游戏加上一堆养眼和悦耳的东西，比如好听的音效，因为人喜欢视觉和听觉刺激。而且通常这种东西越多越好，哪怕很细微，哪怕你看到的游戏只是

cues.en: just a beautiful vista or something. It doesn't have to be explosions and bright fireworks going off everywhere. Although many games take that approach, right? The more of that that we have and the better synced it is to the sound effects, the more compelling the game ends up being. The third thing is how we keep people playing.
cues.zh: 一片美丽的远景之类的。不一定非得是到处爆炸、烟花齐放。虽然很多游戏确实这么做，对吧？这种东西越多、和音效同步得越好，游戏就越有吸引力。第三点是我们如何让人一直玩下去。

cues.en: which is not only do they have a long-term goal that helps them make sense of what they're trying to do, but you break that up into little bite-sized goals. So it doesn't feel like I'm trying to do this epic thing that I don't ever know when I'm going to accomplish it because I have a nearer step, right? So maybe, I don't know, the tank mission isn't a very good one because first-person shooter missions aren't this long, but just imagine that it was an hour-long mission and getting the gas can was the half-hour point, but there was like a five-minute point of like,
cues.zh: 也就是，他们不仅有一个长期目标，能帮他们理解自己在做什么，还要把这个目标拆成一个个小目标。这样就不会觉得“我在做一件史诗级的大事，却永远不知道什么时候能完成”，因为我有更近的一步，对吧？所以，比如，我不知道，坦克任务这个例子不太好，因为第一人称射击任务没这么长，但假设它是一个一小时的任务，拿到汽油罐是半小时节点，但还有个五分钟节点，比如

cues.en: Your first way point is to get up on the tower and scout out where the enemies are. Then you've got to go find the key. And then you've got to get open the warehouse, right? So you add these goals where the player always knows what they can do next. And it's a relatively easy thing. It feels well within their reach. And this keeps people playing. It's like, you know, just one more level. Or if I just do this next thing, I'll be in a good spot so that when I save and go to bed and wake up tomorrow.
cues.zh: 你的第一个路点就是爬上塔楼，侦察敌人在哪里。然后你得去找钥匙。接着你得打开仓库，对吧？所以你加入这些目标，让玩家始终知道自己下一步能做什么。而且这是相对容易的事，感觉完全在他们能力范围内。这就能让人一直玩下去。就像“再来一关”。或者“只要我把下一件事做了，我就会处在好位置，这样等我存档、上床睡觉，明天醒来

cues.en: I'll be in a totally good position to keep going. And of course, they do that one thing, and then there's just one more next thing just within their reach now. And so they keep going and going, and you pull them through the game that way. And the last thing I want to highlight here is this feeling of constant improvement that we've added to games, which comes in many guises. Probably the most familiar one is in role-playing games, where your character has experience points, and you get enough of those, and his stats goes up.
cues.zh: 就能处在完全有利的位置继续玩下去。当然，他们做完那件事，马上又有一个新的下一步，现在正好触手可及。于是他们一直玩下去，你就这样把他们一路带过整个游戏。最后我想强调的是，我们给游戏加入的这种持续成长感，它有很多形式。最熟悉的可能是在角色扮演游戏里，角色有经验值，攒够之后属性就提升。

cues.en: You know, a more Byzantine version of just score that we used to have in arcade games, right? Score provided a feeling of constant improvement because you could play again to get a better score and usually that would work. But now instead of having it be a player skill thing, it's what we call an avatar skill thing.
cues.zh: 你知道，这其实是过去街机游戏里那种分数的更复杂版本，对吧？分数带来一种持续进步感，因为你可以再玩一次拿更高分，而且通常这管用。但现在它不再是玩家技能，而是我们所谓的角色技能。

cues.en: which means it's more of a fictional thing in the game. So you're not improving your own skills. You're improving the fictional skills of something in the game world. You're learning new spells. You're getting more gold pieces. You're getting awesome magic items that glow with fire, lots of eye candy when you run around with them. So hopefully all of that makes sense to everybody, and there's no surprises there. Now, to segue into the next part of the talk, I think it's important to say that this kind of collection and hoarding mechanism, which we see in RPGs,
cues.zh: 这意味着它更多是游戏里的虚构设定。所以你提升的并不是自己的技能，而是在提升游戏世界中某个虚构角色的技能。你学到了新法术，得到了更多金币，拿到了散发着火焰光芒的酷炫魔法物品，带着它们到处跑时特别吸睛。希望大家都能理解这些，这里没什么难懂的。那么，顺着切入接下来的内容，我认为很重要的一点是，这种我们在RPG中见到的收集和囤积机制，

cues.en: originally, but it's starting to spread into a lot of different game types, especially casual games, is the way those rewards are scheduled. We tend to do it with things, if they're not exactly a Skinner box, they very closely resemble a Skinner box. And in case you don't know what a Skinner box is, it's something like this. It's an experimental setup where you have a mouse living in a box, and you can't get out.
cues.zh: 起初只存在于RPG，但现在已经开始蔓延到许多不同类型的游戏中，尤其是休闲游戏，那就是这些奖励的发放排期方式。我们通常采用的做法，就算不完全等同于斯金纳箱（Skinner box），也极其相似。如果你不知道什么是斯金纳箱，它大概长这样：这是一个实验装置，里面有一只关在箱子里出不去的老鼠。

cues.en: And every once in a while, some kind of stimulus plays, like a light goes off or a sound happens or whatever. And during those periods, if the mouse hits a lever, then a food pellet will come out, which, whether it's delicious or whether he's just really hungry, I don't know. But then he learns that, right? And it's a way of training the mouse to perform this activity.
cues.zh: 每隔一段时间，就会出现某种刺激，比如灯亮了或者发出声音之类的。在这些时候，如果老鼠按一下杠杆，就会掉出一颗食物颗粒，至于这东西是美味还是它单纯太饿了，我也不清楚。但老鼠就会学会这一点，对吧？这是一种训练老鼠去执行这种行为的方法，

cues.en: of hitting the lever when a stimulus occurs. And the interesting thing about Skinner boxes is if you give somebody a predictable reward, then the behavior is less well-trained than if you give them a randomized reward, right? So if every time the light goes on and the mouse hits the pellet once or hits the lever once and the food pellet comes out, you know, that kind of works. You can train the mouse to hit the lever, but...
cues.zh: 即在刺激出现时去按杠杆。斯金纳箱有趣的地方在于，如果你给它可预测的奖励，那么这种行为的训练效果，反而不如给它随机奖励来得好，对吧？所以如果每次灯一亮，老鼠按一下杠杆，食物颗粒就掉出来，这种方式确实管用，你能训练老鼠去按杠杆，但是……

cues.en: If he has to hit the lever an unknown amount of times, like a random number between 1 and 10, you're going to really train that mouse to compulsively press this lever when a stimulus happens, right? And probably most of you, oh, and in case you want to like shock the mouse or something, there's like an electric floor. I guess that's if you're really pissed off that he's not learning to press the lever, right? You can do a bunch of different experiments with this kind of setup.
cues.zh: 如果它必须按未知次数的杠杆，比如1到10次之间的随机次数，你就能真正把这只老鼠训练成一旦受到刺激，就会强迫性地狂按这个杠杆，对吧？可能你们大多数人，哦对了，如果你想电击老鼠之类的，底下还有个通电地板。我想那大概是在你为它总学不会按杠杆而抓狂时用的吧？用这种装置你可以做很多种不同的实验。

cues.en: Anyway, you're probably more familiar with Skinner boxes in this kind of context where they don't have electric shot floors. But a slot machine is almost exactly a Skinner box in that it has a randomized reward schedule that's optimized to get you to put as many coins as possible into the slot machine. Or you might be more familiar with them in this context.
cues.zh: 总之，你们可能更熟悉这种场景下的斯金纳箱，这里可没有通电地板。但老虎机几乎就是一个折中意义上的斯金纳箱，它有一套随机的奖励排期，专门优化用来诱导你往老虎机里塞尽可能多的硬币。或者，你们可能在下面这种场景里对它更熟悉。

cues.en: which is a dungeon crawler type of RPG, where every time you open, you know, a barrel or a crate, there's an unknown quantity of treasure inside. It might be completely empty. It might just have a couple of gold pieces and you're like, ah, but it might have like 10 gold pieces and you're like, ah, awesome. You know, I'm really on my way to buying that next level of sword. So anyway, this game design best practices set here is going to be so useful to refer back to that I'm going to put it in a toolbox.
cues.zh: 这是一款地牢探索类RPG：每次你打开木桶或板条箱，里面的宝物数量都是未知的。可能完全是空的，也可能只有几枚金币，你会想“唉”；但有时可能有10枚金币，你就会觉得“哇，太棒了，我离买下一级剑又近了一步”。总之，这里总结的游戏设计最佳实践非常值得回头参考，所以我要把它放进一个工具箱。

cues.en: So I can carry it with us through the rest of the talk. But just remember what this stands for. This is all the good stuff that game designers have learned to do to make games compelling to play and more appealing to more people than the old style games used to be. So how did we arrive? How do we know these are best practices? How did we learn these? There are two ways. One of the ways is very natural. And it's just this process of evolving inspiration that happens in the game designer community.
cues.zh: 这样我就能带着它听完后面的分享。但要记住它代表什么：这些都是游戏设计师总结出的好做法，让游戏更吸引人、能吸引比老式游戏更多的人。那我们是怎么走到这一步的？怎么知道这些是最佳实践？怎么学到的？有两种方式。一种很自然，就是游戏设计师社群中不断演化灵感的这个过程。

cues.en: Most people who want to design games are doing it because they like video games. So they have some particular game that they really liked a lot. And they're like, oh, that game was cool. But you know what? It would be even cooler if the gun was bigger or something. Actually, a real one is it would be really cool if you not only shot people, but you could shoot people with the gun. And you would stake them to the wall, so they're hanging on the wall afterward. Does anyone know that game? Yes. I don't know. Did someone say something else? It was Painkiller did it originally.
cues.zh: 大多数想设计游戏的人，是因为喜欢电子游戏。所以他们会特别钟情某款游戏，觉得“那游戏很酷。但要是枪更大一点，不是更酷吗？”真实例子是：如果不仅能把人射死，还能用枪把人钉在墙上，事后人就挂在墙上，那不是很酷吗？有人知道这游戏吗？对。我不知道。有人说了别的吗？最早做这个的是 Painkiller。

cues.en: Maybe somebody did it before Painkiller, but I don't know what game it is if they did that. So there's this process of taking something you thought was cool or interesting or neat and making it better. And that's a very, I'm going to say, innocent kind of motivation. It's a joyful kind of thing to take something that was there done by your predecessors and kind of stand on the shoulders of giants and make something even better.
cues.zh: 也许在 Painkiller 之前有人做过，但如果有，我也不知道是什么游戏。所以这个过程就是：拿一个你觉得酷、有趣或巧妙的东西，把它做得更好。我会说，这是一种很单纯的动机。拿前人的成果，站在巨人肩膀上做出更好的东西，这是件快乐的事。

cues.en: But over time, as game budgets got bigger and we became more professional, I put that in quotes because it's a word I really don't trust, we learned how to monitor players in a little bit of a better way. Because what was happening in the earlier days, even into the 90s, is we think that our game was great. We did a really good job polishing it. It's better, clearly better, than the previous game.
cues.zh: 但久而久之，游戏预算越来越大，我们也越来越“专业”——我加引号，是因为这个词我不太信——我们学会了用更好的方式观察玩家。因为早期甚至到90年代，情况是：我们觉得自己的游戏很棒，打磨得很好，明显比上一款游戏更好。

cues.en: You sit someone down and they try to play it, and it's totally unplayable. They can't get used to the controls that we got really good at because we're the developers and we've been using the controls for years. They don't understand where they're supposed to go and what they're supposed to be doing when we thought we made all that stuff clear. So the method that we've come up with for dealing with this is to just silently watch players. You sit them down, they start playing your game, and usually they're going to start to have problems. And typically, the way that you deal with that
cues.zh: 可你让人坐下来一玩，完全没法玩。他们适应不了我们习以为常的操作，因为我们是开发者，已经用了好几年。他们不知道该往哪走、该做什么，而我们以为这些都讲清楚了。于是我们想出的办法就是：安静地观察玩家。你让他们坐下，开始玩你的游戏，通常很快就会遇到问题。通常，你应对这种情况的方式

cues.en: Or the instinct for dealing with that is to help them out like, no, no, oh, sorry. We didn't make the HUD for this clear enough. Do this thing or press this button. But you don't do any of that. You don't help them at all. You just sit there and watch them. And it's very painful to sit there and watch them, but you do it. And every time there's a little glitch or they get confused, you write it down. And that gives you your to-do list for when you go and work on your game later.
cues.zh: 或者说应对这种情况的本能，就是去帮他们，比如“不不，哦抱歉，这个 HUD 我们没做清楚。做这个，或者按这个按钮”。但这些都不要做。你完全不帮他们，就坐在那里看着。坐在那看非常痛苦，但你还是得做。每次出现小故障或他们困惑时，你就记下来。这就成了你之后回去改游戏时的待办清单。

cues.en: I will say a little more scientific way of designing games than the first way than just what I think would be cool, right? Because it involves empirical observation and then responding to those observations. I have to find where I am in my notes because I haven't been using them. OK. So imagine I've done all this, and I'm making some modern game, and it's a dungeon crawler game. And it employs a bunch of those things from that best practices toolbox, right? So it's got a
cues.zh: 我觉得相比第一种只凭“我觉得很酷”的做法，这种设计游戏的方式要更科学一些，对吧？因为它包含了实证观察，并针对这些观察做出调整。我得看一下讲稿看到哪了，因为我刚才一直没看。好。设想一下我把这些都做到了，我正在做一款现代游戏，它是一款地牢探险游戏。而且它用到了那个“最佳实践工具箱”里的很多东西，对吧？所以它有

cues.en: treadmill of player stats that just go up and up and up and equipment stats you can get better and better swords and armor and all many different categories of equipment right and the equipment prices go up and maybe you need gems for some of them and maybe you need gems to like instill capabilities in different weapons and then you kind of want to reclaim those gems right so it's kind of an intricate ecology of these improving stats on many different kinds of
cues.zh: 不断向上攀升的玩家属性跑步机，还有装备属性，你能拿到越来越好的刀剑和护甲，以及各种不同类别的装备，对吧？装备价格水涨船高，有的可能还需要宝石，可能需要宝石来给不同的武器赋予能力，然后你又想把那些宝石拆卸回收，对吧？所以这形成了一个相当错综复杂的生态系统，包含了游戏中各种不同

cues.en: objects in the game, right? Then, like I said, we'll have a loot skinner box where you kill a monster and a random reward pops out of the monster, or you open a chest and a random reward pops out. We have all these cool explosion effects and weapon trails and, like, you know, lightning strikes and stuff like that. And we have all these little five-minute quest milestones, so you always have a very tangible next thing to do. And we have this epic story about how there's this evil guy, the fusil, who you have to go kill in the end, and you're the only person who can do it, right?
cues.zh: 物品的属性提升，对吧？然后，就像我说的，我们还会做一个掉落斯金纳箱，你杀死一只怪，怪身上就会掉出随机奖励，或者你开个宝箱，就会爆出随机奖励。我们还有各种酷炫的爆炸特效、武器拖尾，以及类似雷击之类的效果。我们还有很多5分钟的任务里程碑，让你总能清晰地知道下一步该做什么。而且我们还有一个史诗般的故事，讲的是最终有个叫 Fusil 的大反派需要你去消灭，而你是唯一能做到的人，对吧？

cues.en: So we do all those things. And we have a very compelling game. We know that. We can almost manufacture these off an assembly line now. But now do a certain thought experiment, where you take that big list of things that I just said and take the same game, but strip all those items out of that game. So no big story about the fusil. And no five-minute quest milestones. They can be functionally there, but just don't put them in in a player-leading kind of way. You take out the loot skinner box.
cues.zh: 把这些全做了。我们就能做出一款非常引人入胜的游戏。这点我们很清楚。我们现在几乎可以用流水线把它们量产出来。但现在我们来做个思想实验，列出我刚才说的这一大串东西，拿同一款游戏，但把所有这些元素全部剥离出去。不要 Fusil 的宏大史诗故事。不要5分钟的任务里程碑。它们在功能上可以存在，但不要以那种牵着玩家鼻子走的方式放进去。拿掉掉落斯金纳箱，

cues.en: and replace it with typical game balance, you take out all the non-necessary special effects, you make it something like chess. So chess is an abstract game. It doesn't particularly have eye candy or special effects. It certainly doesn't have an epic story. But it's considered to be a very compelling game. There's a core of chess that doesn't need anything from that toolbox that has fascinated people for many, many years.
cues.zh: 把它替换成常规的游戏平衡，拿掉所有不必要的特效，把它做成类似于国际象棋那样的东西。国际象棋是一种抽象游戏。它并没有什么抓人眼球的视效或特效。它当然也没有史诗故事。但它被认为是一款极具吸引力的游戏。国际象棋有一个核心，它不需要那个工具箱里的任何东西，却吸引了人们很多很多年。

cues.en: So imagine the dungeon crawl version of chess. What would that game be? And I don't mean game mechanically. I mean stripped down. Here's a graph. So in these games, I mentioned the word treadmill a couple slides ago. The way these are very intentionally designed is we want the player to feel more and more powerful, and like he's having progress. So he gets experience points, and he gets better equipment and all that.
cues.zh: 所以想象一下地牢探险版的国际象棋。那会是一款怎样的游戏？我指的不是游戏机制层面。我是指剥离一切之后的样子。这是一张图表。在这些游戏中，我几张幻灯片前提到过“跑步机”这个词。这些游戏之所以被非常刻意地设计成这样，是因为我们想让玩家觉得自己越来越强，感觉自己一直在进步。于是他获得了经验值，拿到了更好的装备等等。

cues.en: You know, if the monsters didn't get harder too, then the game would become trivial easy after like 15 minutes, because we really pumped stats through the ceiling, right? So what you do is you have them encounter harder and harder monsters over time, and the two go up roughly in parity, right? So what happens is if you graph the difficulty of the game over time, it's probably something like this, assuming the designer was reasonably skilled, where it starts out kind of easy, and then it ramps up after a sort of futorial phase, and then it kind of oscillates for a bit.
cues.zh: 你知道，如果怪物不变难，那游戏大概15分钟后就会变得特别简单，因为我们的属性实在堆得太高了，对吧？所以你要做的就是让玩家随着时间遇到越来越难的怪物，两边大致同步上升，对吧？结果就是，如果你把游戏难度随时间画成图，假设设计师水平还行，大概会是这样：一开始比较简单，经过一段教程阶段后开始爬升，然后会波动一阵。

cues.en: This line, this dotted line across the middle, is sort of what we think of as the difficulty of the game on average. And note that we actually don't make the difficulty lock to that line and go horizontally. And the reason is because that doesn't feel that good. Instead, we set up a bit of an oscillation around this. So you have periods of intensity, and then periods of relaxation, and periods of intensity, and periods of relaxation. This provides for a sense of drama in the game play.
cues.zh: 中间这条虚线，大概就是我们理解的整体平均难度。注意，我们并不会让难度锁死在这条线上水平前进。原因是这样手感不太好。相反，我们会围绕它设置一些波动。于是你有紧张期，然后放松期，再紧张，再放松。这能让玩法更有戏剧感。

cues.en: actually allowing the player to feel powerful, right? Because if monsters are always perfectly matched to you, you never get to feel like this awesome sword that you got or the fact that you're level 17 matters, right? But if you feel more powerful for a little bit, and then that gradually wears away, people won't notice. So in some sense, this curve is about creating drama, and in some sense, it's about fooling the player into feeling like the treadmill is more real than it is.
cues.zh: 其实也让玩家感觉自己很强，对吧？因为如果怪物永远和你完美匹配，你就永远感受不到刚拿到的那把好剑有多厉害，或者自己17级这件事有什么意义，对吧？但如果你先觉得自己强了一阵，然后这种感觉逐渐消退，人们就不会注意到。所以某种意义上，这条曲线是在制造戏剧性；某种意义上，也是在骗玩家，让他们觉得这个刷怪跑步机比实际更真实。

cues.en: Anyway, so while you're doing all the stripping down of this game, you might as well downgrade the graphics, because that's all eye candy. It's not really necessary. So you probably get something that looks like an indie game. But it's all functional. You can make the same game out of all that. So after you've done this, go take a poll. Game companies love to ask people what they want. You go take a poll of how many people want to play this game versus how many people want to play the awesome looking
cues.zh: 总之，当你把这游戏这样一层层剥到最后时，不妨也把画面降级，因为那些都只是视觉糖衣，并不是必需的。所以你大概会得到一个看起来像独立游戏的东西，但功能都还在。你可以用这些做出同样的游戏。做完这些后，去做个调查。游戏公司特别喜欢问人们想要什么。你去调查一下，有多少人想玩这个游戏，对比有多少人想玩你一开始那个画面惊艳的

cues.en: AAA game that you started with. And what you find is very few people want to play this stripped down game. Some people might. Very, very hardcore gamers might do it. But you lose most of your audience. That's all I'm going to say about that at the moment. Now, RPGs are a very complicated genre of game. Like I said, they have all these intertwining things that we've learned how to weave together.
cues.zh: 3A游戏。结果你会发现，很少有人想玩这个被剥简后的游戏。有些人可能会。非常非常硬核的玩家也许会。但你会失去大部分受众。关于这点我现在就说到这里。现在，RPG是非常复杂的一类游戏。就像我说的，它们有所有这些相互交织的东西，而我们已经学会了如何把它们编织在一起。

cues.en: create player motivation. So you can run this exercise again with a much simpler thing. And this might help convince you that what I'm saying makes sense. Or it might help make the model make more sense. So think about slot machines again. Imagine doing the same stripping down process to a slot machine. So you get rid of all the flashing lights and ringing bells and sounds and stuff.
cues.zh: 来创造玩家动机。所以你可以用一个简单得多的东西再做一遍这个练习。这也许能帮你相信我说的话有道理，或者帮这个模型更容易理解。再想想老虎机。想象对老虎机做同样的剥简过程。你去掉所有闪烁的灯光、响铃、声音之类的东西。

cues.en: You know, you also get rid of the Skinner box, right? So you get rid of that reward schedule I was talking about. So you don't actually ever win any money from this slot machine. And just to make it fair, you don't put any coins in either. And it's actually better because now you don't lose money ever, whereas with a real slot machine, you're guaranteed to lose money over time. So this is a 100% improvement over the traditional slot machine functionally, right? So all that happens now...
cues.zh: 你看，你还去掉了斯金纳箱，对吧？也就是去掉了我刚才说的奖励机制。所以你根本不会从这台老虎机里赢到一分钱。而且为了公平起见，你也不用投任何硬币。这其实更好，因为你永远不会输钱，而面对真正的老虎机，随着时间推移你注定会输光。所以从功能上讲，这比传统老虎机提升了100%，对吧？那现在会发生什么呢……

cues.en: We've gotten rid of all these things. So it's a relatively plain looking box with still the dials in there with different shapes on it. And you pull the lever and the shapes spin. And either they match and the slot machine says, hey, you won. Or they don't match and the slot machine says, oh, you didn't win. But whether you win or didn't win, you don't win anything and you don't lose anything. So how many people would play that slot machine? You might play with it for a second as a novelty, but it's not something that people are going to be mobbing into casinos to play.
cues.zh: 我们去掉了所有这些机制。所以它成了一个看起来平平无奇的盒子，里面依然有带不同图案的转盘。你拉下拉杆，图案开始旋转。要么图案匹配，老虎机提示说，嘿，你赢了。要么不匹配，老虎机提示说，噢，你没赢。但无论你赢没赢，你都没赢到任何东西，也没输掉任何东西。那么会有多少人玩这种老虎机呢？你可能会出于新鲜感玩上一会儿，但绝不会有人为了玩它而挤爆赌场。

cues.en: And more to the point, it's not going to be something that, you know, state and national governments feel threatened enough by socially that they have to regulate it or outlaw it, right? Because it's become, by the time you take away the rewards schedule, it's become a totally different device, even though mechanically it's the same device, right? So all those designer best practices that I was talking about can take something that's inherently boring and pointless, like a box where you pull a lever and don't really win anything,
cues.zh: 更关键的是，它也不会让各州和国家政府在社会层面感到威胁，以至于非要去监管甚至取缔它，对吧？因为一旦拿掉奖励机制，尽管机械结构完全相同，它也变成了一种截然不同的装置，对吧？所以，我之前提到的那些设计师的最佳实践，可以让原本枯燥无味、毫无意义的东西——比如一个拉下拉杆却什么都赢不到的盒子——

cues.en: and turn it into something that's compulsive, compelling. And the thing is, we can do this with video games as well, and not just slot machines. In a sense, we figured out a way to engineer our way around boredom and take a relatively pointless game that's just about clicking on things and not doing anything real and adding production values to it and turning it into something that a lot of people want to play. And this is key.
cues.zh: 变成让人欲罢不能、极其引人入胜的东西。问题在于，我们不仅能在老虎机上做到这点，在电子游戏上也同样适用。在某种意义上，我们找到了一种用工程手段绕过无聊的方法，把一个只是点点东西、没有任何现实意义的无聊游戏，通过堆叠制作水准，变成无数人争着玩的东西。这一点至关重要。

cues.en: We've engineered our way around boredom to a certain point. And I'm focusing on boredom right now, but we've engineered our way around some other things. We've engineered our way around frustration by just learning how to tune games really well and doing that player watching stuff that we saw before. Every time someone gets frustrated, like, oh, I can't beat this monster, you just make that level easier. So you iron out all these bumps, and eventually you get a very smooth play experience that a lot of people want to participate in.
cues.zh: 我们在一定程度上用工程手段绕过了无聊。我现在重点在说无聊，但我们其实还绕过了其他一些东西。我们学会了如何精细调校游戏，并运用前面提到的玩家观察法，用工程手段绕过了挫败感。每当有人感到挫败，比如“哎呀，我打不过这个怪”，你就把那关改简单点。通过抚平所有这些颠簸，最终就能提供一种极其丝滑、吸引大众参与的游戏体验。

cues.en: And we keep doing this in video games is keep getting better and better and more fun. And we all live happily ever after the end, right? Probably not. I certainly have issues with this. And I know other people who do as well. I said that we're engineering our way around boredom. What does that mean, really? I mean, there's a very obvious surface meaning to it. But what effect does that have? What does it really do? And to answer that, you have to know, well, what is boredom, right?
cues.zh:
我们在电子游戏里不断这样做，游戏就变得越来越好、越来越有趣。
然后我们都从此过上幸福生活，对吧？
大概不会。
我本人对此肯定有意见。
我知道别人也有同感。
我说过，我们正在用工程手段绕开无聊。
这到底是什么意思？
我是说，它有个非常明显的表面含义。
但它会带来什么影响？
它到底起了什么作用？
要回答这个问题，你得先知道：无聊到底是什么，对吧？

cues.en: People don't like boredom, they don't like thinking about boredom, they don't like being bored. But boredom is actually a healthy response to unproductive situations, right? Human beings have boredom as a response because of evolution, right? Boredom has survival value.
cues.zh:
人们不喜欢无聊，不喜欢思考无聊，也不喜欢感到无聊。
但无聊其实是对没有产出的情境的一种健康反应，对吧？
人类因为进化而把无聊作为一种反应，对吧？
无聊有生存价值。

cues.en: What it's for is you get into a situation that's unproductive. Your senses aren't being stimulated. You're not learning anything about your new environment. You're just being surrounded by the same old stuff. And you get bored, and you start getting jumpy and agitated, and that causes you to want to go do something new or go do something different. It causes you to go outside of your normal behavior patterns.
cues.zh:
它的作用是这样：你陷入一个没有产出的情境。
你的感官没有被刺激。
你没有学到关于新环境的任何东西。
你只是被同样的旧东西包围。
然后你感到无聊，开始变得坐立不安、烦躁，这会让你想去尝试新事物或做点不同的事。
它会让你跳出正常的行为模式。

cues.en: Hopefully, a lot of us are computer scientists in here. So if you're familiar with the hill climbing process, what happens in hill climbing is you'll often start going up a hill and then you get stuck at a local maximum, right? And you can think of boredom for human beings to vastly oversimplify the situation as being something like adding a simulated annealing step into your hill climbing process to allow you to get unstuck.
cues.zh:
希望这里很多人都是计算机科学家。
所以，如果你熟悉爬山过程，爬山时你常常会开始爬上一座山，然后卡在局部最大值，对吧？
你可以把人类的无聊——极大地简化一下——想成类似在爬山过程中加入一个模拟退火步骤，让你脱离卡住的状态。

cues.en: You're in a place that's pretty good. You're not in any imminent danger or whatever. But you're bored. You start doing different stuff. And it jumps you around this graph to different places. And eventually, one of the places you jump may allow you to climb higher. So here's the point. Imagine that for some reason, we're playing that stripped down version of the RPG that has none of the graphics and none of the player stats or anything. And in fact, it's so stripped down that looking at this graph, when you kill a monster,
cues.zh:
你处在一个相当不错的地方。
你没有任何迫在眉睫的危险之类的。
但你无聊了。
你开始做不同的事。
它会把你在这个图上跳到不同位置。
最终，你跳到的一个位置可能让你爬得更高。
所以重点在这里。
想象一下，出于某种原因，我们在玩那个精简版 RPG，它没有画面，也没有玩家属性之类的东西。
事实上，它精简到这种程度：看着这张图，当你杀死一个怪物时，

cues.en: Normally, in an RPG, you get loot and maybe some items and some experience points, which are all different progression things. Those are really just different ways of bumping you slightly along this drama curve toward the end of the game. They just do it in a way such that they camouflage that that's what's happening. Well, just get rid of all that stuff. Every time you kill a monster, it just disappears without even a sound effect, because you know it disappeared. You don't see it anymore. And then you just slightly bump a pointer along this drama curve a little bit.
cues.zh:
通常，在 RPG 里，你会获得战利品，可能还有一些物品和经验值，它们都是不同的成长要素。
那些其实只是不同方式，让你沿着这条剧情曲线稍微向游戏结局推进。
它们只是用某种方式掩盖了正在发生的事。
好吧，把这些东西全去掉。
每次你杀死一个怪物，它就只是消失，甚至连音效都没有，因为你知道它消失了。
你再也看不到它。
然后你只是沿着这条剧情曲线稍微拨动一下指针。

cues.en: So you do all that, and for some reason, you found someone who's still playing this game. To use this sort of an example case for another thought experiment, right? And then you reverse that process, and you add in all the production values to create something that's compelling, right? So it's not just the fact that we've engineered our way around boredom, but we've
cues.zh: 做完这一切后，由于某种原因，你发现居然还有人在玩这款游戏。我们以此为例再做个思想实验，对吧？然后你把这个过程反过来，注入全部的制作心血，去打造出真正吸引人的东西，对吧？所以这不仅是我们巧妙地绕开了无聊，更是我们

cues.en: taken this evolutionary mechanism that was a defense for human beings, that was a way, a thing that they use to increase their survival value, to improve their quality of life, and were redirecting it. So instead of improving things about their own quality of life, they're now improving imaginary things in an imaginary world. But they're still exerting time and effort. It's just the effort is going somewhere different now.
cues.zh: 劫持了这种演化机制，它本是人类的一种防御手段，一种用来提升生存价值、改善生活质量的本能，而我们却转移了它的方向。因此，他们不再去改善自己现实生活中的品质，而是在虚拟世界里去升级虚构的事物。但他们依然在付出时间和精力，只是这些付出如今流向了别处。

cues.en: Now, in the process of going somewhere different, what happens to it? Well, a lot of it just is in this imaginary world, but some of it goes into the game designer's and game publisher's wallet in the form of whatever, maybe a micropayment, maybe the price of the game and whatnot. So if you think about this objectively, engineering your way through a human defense and then profiting by that is a parasitic form of behavior.
cues.zh: 那么，在流向别处的过程中，这些付出又变成了什么？很大一部分就留在了这个虚构的世界里，但还有一部分则以微交易、游戏售价等形式，流入了游戏设计师和发行商的钱包。所以客观来看，攻破人类的防御机制并以此牟利，本质上就是一种寄生行为。

cues.en: But I'm a game designer, and I don't necessarily want to think of myself as a parasite. And a lot of game designers, if you were to say this to them, they would say, well, hey, we're not parasites because people genuinely enjoy our games. And they pay us for what we do voluntarily. But maybe those ants, the subjects of parasitic mind control at the beginning of the video, maybe they're really enjoying themselves while they hang from that purple flower and get eaten.
cues.zh: 但我是一名游戏设计师，我可不想把自己当成寄生虫。如果你把这番话告诉很多游戏设计师，他们会说：“嘿，我们才不是寄生虫，因为大家是真心喜欢我们的游戏，他们也是自愿为我们的劳动付钱的。”但也许在视频开头那些被寄生虫精神控制的蚂蚁，在挂在紫花上被吃掉时，其实也挺自得其乐的呢。

cues.en: The fact of whether they're enjoying themselves or not is almost immaterial to whether something devious is going on. But taking a measured view toward this and not just trying to flog it for controversy, I do find that even if you believe this argument that what we're doing is circumventing human defenses, it's not necessarily a bad thing. We circumvent human defenses for good purposes all the time.
cues.zh: 它们到底享不享受，几乎完全不影响这背后是否存在某种险恶的勾当。但如果理性看待这件事，而不只是为了博眼球造争议，我确实觉得，就算你认同我们在绕过人类防御机制这个观点，它也未必是件坏事。我们出于良善的目的绕过人类防御机制的情况比比皆是。

cues.en: So say for whatever reason your liver's failing and you need to get a transplant, you go to the doctor, he'll operate on you, and what does he do? Well, he circumvents his way through your pain defense by giving you some anesthetics. He cuts you open with a scalpel. He jiggers around in there. And then hopefully you're better at the end of that process. And you give him some money. He takes that money and puts it in his wallet. But you can think of a parallel situation.
cues.zh: 比方说，不管出于什么原因，你的肝衰竭了需要做移植手术，你去看医生，医生要给你做手术，他会怎么做？他给你注射麻醉剂，绕开了你的疼痛防御机制；他用手术刀切开你的身体，在里面摆弄一番；最终但愿你能康复。然后你付给他钱，他把钱揣进钱包。不过，你也可以想想另一种类似的情况。

cues.en: or parallel in many ways, where you're just in a bar and you're trying to get home at night and there's a mugger there and at first he gets around your social defenses, maybe just by hiding or by appearing to be unthreatening until you get close and then he gets through your physical defenses, you know, and he cuts you open with a knife and takes some money of yours and puts it in his wallet, right? They're very similar situations, but the ultimate difference really is whether this process
cues.zh: 或者说，这在很多方面都很相似：你就在酒吧里，晚上想回家，那儿有个劫匪，一开始他绕过你的社交防线，也许只是靠躲藏，或者装得没有威胁，直到你靠近，然后他突破你的身体防线，你知道，他用刀划开你，拿走你一些钱，放进自己的钱包，对吧？这些情况非常相似，但最终的区别其实在于，这个过程

cues.en: of circumventing the defenses and getting the money in response was of benefit to the person being circumvented or was harmful to the person being circumvented. My first thought when I was thinking about this was, well, maybe it doesn't really have to do with benefit and harm. Maybe it's just about whether it's voluntary or not. Like you hopefully voluntarily went to the doctor. And you hopefully didn't voluntarily get mugged. But we can do another thought experiment.
cues.zh: 绕过防线并因此拿到钱，到底是对被绕过防线的人有利，还是对被绕过防线的人有害。我刚开始想这个问题时，第一反应是：嗯，也许它其实跟有利和有害无关。也许只跟是不是自愿有关。比如你希望自己是自愿去看医生的。也希望自己不是自愿被抢劫的。但我们可以再做另一个思想实验。

cues.en: to prove that that's not the case. So imagine there's some confidence man. You don't know he's a confidence man. You just meet him out on the street and he's like, oh, my wife's sick and I've got to go get on a plane to go take care of her. But I lost my wallet and it had my plane ticket and all my credit cards in it. But I need money to go see her right now. And I've got this really nice watch. It's a gold watch, surely at a pawn shop.
cues.zh: 来证明事实并非如此。那么想象有一个骗子。你不知道他是骗子。你只是在街上遇到他，他说：哦，我妻子病了，我得坐飞机去照顾她。但我丢了钱包，里面有我的机票和所有信用卡。可我现在就需要钱去看她。我有这块特别好的表。是金表，在当铺肯定能收。

cues.en: You could get $200 for it. So why don't you give me $100 right now, and then I can go get on the plane, and you'll make a profit, and everybody's happy. And he's very convincing. He has a great personality, so you believe him. You give him $100, he'll give you the watch, and five minutes later, you're down the street at the pawn shop. By the way, he's jumped in a cab, and he's gone ostensibly to the airport. And at the pawn shop, you find out the watch is fake. And you got ripped off. But you voluntarily entered into that business transaction. But it's still a crime. It's still fraud. He still did something.
cues.zh: 你能卖到200美元。那你现在为什么不给我100美元，然后我就能去赶飞机，你还能赚一笔，大家都开心。他非常有说服力。他很有魅力，所以你就信了他。你给他100美元，他把表给你，五分钟后，你到了街那头的当铺。顺便说一句，他已经跳上一辆出租车，表面上是去机场了。而在当铺，你发现表是假的。你被坑了。但你是自愿进入这笔交易的。但这仍然是犯罪。仍然是诈骗。他还是做了某件事。

cues.en: that was a crime, right? So let's extend this thought experiment. Let's think of another confidence man. He's a little better than the earlier guy, right? And he plays for higher stakes. He works on Wall Street, and he offers to invest your money for five years and give you great returns at the end of that five years. And you're like, sounds great. I've got this money in the bank. Didn't know what to do with it. Now I know. So you give him $100,000.
cues.zh: 那是犯罪，对吧？那我们把这个思想实验再扩展一下。再想另一个骗子。他比前面那个人更厉害一点，对吧？而且他玩的赌注更大。他在华尔街工作，提出帮你投资五年，并在五年结束时给你很高的回报。你说：听起来很棒。我银行里正好有这笔钱。之前不知道该拿它怎么办。现在知道了。于是你给了他10万美元。

cues.en: And he goes, gets in a cab, and goes away. And unbeknownst to you, he gets on a plane and flies to Thailand to live off your money for the rest of his life. But he has an assistant who, every month for the five years, mails you a statement with an imaginary number in it that's getting higher and higher, showing that, yes, your money is creating profit. And you're going to be really happy at the end of these five years. And so you're happy.
cues.zh: 然后他走了，上了一辆出租车，离开了。而你并不知道，他上了飞机，飞到泰国，靠你的钱过完余生。但他有个助理，在五年里的每个月都给你寄一份对账单，上面有个虚构的数字，而且越来越高，显示你的钱确实在产生利润。五年后你会非常开心。于是你很开心。

cues.en: over the intervening time. And of course the five years expires, and the guys know where to be seen, and you realize that all your money has been stolen, and then you're very unhappy at the end of that period. So now there's a crime, but you didn't know it was a crime for a long time, but it's still pretty bad. $100,000, I don't want that stolen. But again, you voluntarily entered into that.
cues.zh: 在这中间的岁月里。当然，五年期满了，那些人却不见踪影，你才意识到自己的钱全被卷走了，到头来你非常痛苦。所以这确实构成犯罪，但你很久都不知道这是犯罪，可它依然相当恶劣。十万美元，我可不想被人偷走。但话又说回来，你是自愿参与进去的。

cues.en: You didn't have a problem with it for a while, right? But it's still a crime. So while I'm still in the midst of this whole foray here, just to remind of the point that I'm trying to make is that I'm saying that, at least in the context of game design, what I want to think about is benefit versus harm and not voluntary versus involuntary. So the third case, he's maybe the best confidence man of all, right? And he makes a deal with you. You enter into some kind of nebulous business arrangement with him.
cues.zh: 有一段时间你觉得完全没问题，对吧？但它依然是犯罪。所以趁我还没偏离这个话题，我想提醒大家我要表达的观点是：至少在游戏设计的语境下，我更想探讨的是利与弊，而非自愿与非自愿。至于第三种情况，他可能是最厉害的骗子，对吧？他和做了一笔交易。你和他达成了一种模棱两可的商业合作。

cues.en: And there's never anything clearly wrong. He's just so good at taking things from you in a very, very subtle way that you never notice, just little droplets of money at a time, that you never figure out that anything's happened for five years, 10 years, 20 years, your whole life, right? You live to be 75, 85, 95, whatever is a good old age when you're old, right? And you die happy.
cues.zh: 而且表面上挑不出任何明显的毛病。他只是太擅长用极其隐蔽的方式搜刮你，以至于你毫无察觉，每次只是一点点毛毛雨，你整整5年、10年、20年，甚至一辈子都没发现有任何不对劲，对吧？你活到75岁、85岁、95岁，不管是多大年纪，反正算是高寿了，对吧？而且你死得很安详。

cues.en: But the fact is that you actually die kind of poor, and you actually could have been much richer if this guy hadn't been stealing money from you for your whole life. But he was so good at it that you never even imagined that anything was wrong. You never imagined that you could have had more money and lived a more healthy, fulfilled life with that money if you know how to spend money properly. So it's not even the realization that you were wrong that makes it a crime, right? There's something about
cues.zh: 但事实是，你临死时其实挺穷的，要不是这家伙一辈子都在偷你的钱，你本可以富有得多。但他手段太高明了，你甚至从未想过会出什么问题。你从未想过自己本可以拥有更多财富，懂得合理消费的话，还能靠这些钱过上更健康、更充实的生活。所以，甚至不需要你意识到自己受害，它本身就已经是犯罪了，对吧？问题在于

cues.en: people mistreating people that make something a crime, or that makes it unethical, or however you want to think about that. So, to start to lead into where that's going, the way I feel about games is there's sort of a spectrum, right? There are many spectra, but the one I want to talk about has on the left here games that have some kind of core to them that are intrinsically meaningful, like chess. You can strip away all those designer best practices, and chess is still a very compelling, interesting game, right?
cues.zh: 人与人之间的伤害才让某件事成为犯罪，或者说违背道德，不管你怎么理解都行。那么，为了切入正题，我对游戏的看法是，它大致存在一个光谱，对吧？虽然有许多种维度，但我想聊的这个光谱，左边是具有某种核心机制、本质上富有意义的游戏，比如国际象棋。就算剥离掉所有那些所谓的设计师最佳实践，国际象棋依然是一款非常引人入胜、有趣的游戏，对吧？

cues.en: And then all the way on the right side of the spectrum are games where if you stripped away all that stuff, they're basically completely meaningless. Nobody in their right mind would really want to play them. And obviously, there are lots of points in between that games can occupy. To pick another example, besides chess, we'll go to Go, which is even more minimalistic than chess. It has even simpler rules. It uses absolutely none of the best practices from that toolbox, and yet many people will tell you it's the greatest game ever made.
cues.zh: 而在光谱的最右端，则是那些一旦剥离掉外在包装，本质上就毫无意义的游戏。任何脑子清醒的人都不会真的想去玩。显然，在这两者之间还存在着许多游戏所处的位置。再举一个除国际象棋之外的例子，比如围棋，它比国际象棋还要极简。它的规则甚至更简单。它完全没用到那套工具箱里的任何最佳实践，然而很多人依然会告诉你，它是有史以来最伟大的游戏。

cues.en: Obviously, these best practices are not about making an inherently good game. They're about something else. They're orthogonal to whether the game is good. They're about convincing people to pay attention to your game and want to play it, and about giving them feelings of compulsion regarding your game or not. And when I put things on the spectrum, I don't even think this is an absolute property of games, that some of them are inherently
cues.zh: 显然，这些最佳实践并不是为了做出一款本质上优秀的游戏。它们关注的是别的东西。它们跟游戏好不好是完全正交的两个维度。它们的目的在于吸引人们关注你的游戏并想去玩它，在于让人对你的游戏产生强迫感。而当我把这些放到光谱上衡量时，我甚至不觉得这是游戏的一种绝对属性，即某些游戏本质上就是如此，

cues.en: that everybody should evaluate these games the same on this spectrum. Because part of a game's value to you is whether it brings you a new experience, whether it makes you think about something in a new way. And the first time you play a certain kind of game, it probably does bring you a new experience. So even something like FarmVille is probably cool to play for like five or 10 minutes. But for most people, most of the time, I would say that it lands
cues.zh: 也不觉得每个人在光谱上对这些游戏的评价都应该一致。因为游戏对你的部分价值，在于它能否给你带来全新的体验，能否让你以一种全新的方式去思考某件事。当你第一次玩某种类型的游戏时，它很可能会带给你新体验。所以哪怕像 FarmVille 这样的游戏，玩个五到十分钟可能也挺有意思的。但对大多数人、在大多数时候而言，我觉得它所处的位置，

cues.en: about as far toward the right side of the spectrum as you can get, although history keeps marching on and we'll see what game developers come up with 10 years from now. So my point with the spectrum is even though everybody's different and everybody has different opinions about what's valuable in a game or what they liked about a game or what's cool about it, it still is possible.
cues.zh: 差不多已经尽量偏向光谱的最右端了，尽管历史在不断向前推进，我们还得看看十年后游戏开发者能搞出些什么花样。所以我想借这个光谱表达的是，尽管每个人都各不相同，每个人对游戏中什么有价值、喜欢什么、觉得什么很酷都有不同的看法，但我们依然有可能

cues.en: to generally classify things and generally make judgments about things, not only as an audience, but as a game designer. I can look at a spectrum and say, I really want my work to be over here. I don't want my work to land over here. So just because people have different opinions doesn't make that impossible. Now, there's a reason I bring up FarmVille, and it's because it's really bugging me lately. A few years ago, I gave a talk about World of Warcraft and how I thought that was pretty much a bad idea.
cues.zh: 对事物进行大体的归类和评判，不仅作为受众如此，作为游戏设计师亦然。我可以看着这个光谱说，我真的很希望自己的作品处于这一侧，我不希望它落到那一侧。因此，大家看法不一并不意味着这不可能做到。至于我为什么要提 FarmVille，是因为它最近真的很让我困扰。几年前，我做过一场关于 World of Warcraft 的演讲，谈到为什么我觉得那基本是个糟糕的想法。

cues.en: way worse, actually, not only because it has a bigger audience of more mainstream people, but because of the way it operates intentionally, the way FarmVille is designed to operate is much more dastardly than the way World of Warcraft is designed to operate. And to explain this, I'm going to read a quote from Ian Bogost, who's a professor at Georgia Tech. And he made a game called Cow Clicker, which is a parody of these kind of FarmVille games, which we'll look at in a second.
cues.zh: 实际上这还要恶劣得多，不仅是因为它的受众更广、更主流，更是因为它的运作意图；FarmVille 的机制设计比 World of Warcraft 要卑鄙得多。为了解释这一点，我想引用佐治亚理工学院教授 Ian Bogost 的一段话。他曾做过一款叫 Cow Clicker 的游戏，用来恶搞 FarmVille 这类游戏，我们稍后就会看到。

cues.en: The way he explains it is, many of today's, he starts by talking about traditional single player console games, right? Many of today's console games exert a time crush. They demand tens or even hundreds of hours of attention to complete, some or most of which often feels empty. In that respect, one could argue that many games seem to destroy time. But social games do something even more violent. They also destroy the time we spend away from them through obligation, worry, and dread over missed opportunities.
cues.zh: 他是这么解释的：当今许多……他先从传统的单人主机游戏谈起，对吧？当今许多主机游戏都在残酷地挤压时间。通关它们需要耗费数十甚至数百小时的注意力，而其中部分或大部分时间往往让人感到空虚。从这个角度来看，有人可能会说许多游戏似乎都在毁灭时间。但社交游戏所做的更加残暴。它们通过义务感、担忧以及对错失良机的恐惧，连我们在离开游戏后的时间也一并摧毁了。

cues.en: Now, if you haven't played these games, you might not know how they do it. Hopefully, some of you in this room have not played these games. This is Frontierville, which is a new version of Farmville that was launched recently. And just like a dungeon crawler RPG has a lot of different things woven into it to get you to behave in certain ways, so also does this game. And it's insidious in a few different ways. It's got this little energy bar up at the top with the lightning bolt.
cues.zh: 如果你没玩过这些游戏，可能不知道它们是怎么运作的。但愿在座的各位里有人没玩过。这是 Frontierville，是 Farmville 最近刚推出的新版本。就像地牢探险类 RPG 会融入各种设计来引导你的行为一样，这款游戏也是如此。而且它的手段在好几个方面都非常阴险。比如顶部有一个带闪电图标的体力条。

cues.en: That's how many moves you have, right? And you can spend all those moves probably in one or two minutes, but it's not enough to really accomplish everything you wanted to do when you sat down to work on your farm. So you've got to wait for the moves to refill, but they don't refill very fast, right? It takes probably, you know, I don't know exactly how long, but it's probably three or four hours for that bar to fill all the way up, right? So you want to spend those moves before the bar fills up, but the problem is if you go to sleep or you go watch a movie or something like that,
cues.zh: 那就是你的行动步数，对吧？你大概一两分钟就能把这些步数全用光，但这根本不够完成你坐下来打理农场时想做的一切。所以你就得等步数恢复，但恢复得又特别慢，对吧？大概需要，呃，我也不确切知道多久，但可能要三四个小时才能彻底回满，对吧？所以你会想在能量条回满前把步数花掉，可问题是，如果你去睡个觉或者去看场电影之类的，

cues.en: You're going to start wasting moves because the bar is going to fill up at 14 here in this picture and then you just won't get any more turns after that. So it's like you want to check in with Frontierville every three hours and spend your moves because otherwise your farm is just not getting as good as it would get otherwise. The other thing it does that's pretty evil is that crops wither in this game. So you plant crops. The way it works is you buy a crop for a certain amount of money. You go plant it. You come back later and harvest it and you get more money.
cues.zh: 你就会开始浪费步数，因为像截图里这样，能量条到 14 点就满了，之后你就不会再获得任何步数了。所以你每隔三小时就想打开 Frontierville 签个到，把步数用掉，不然你的农场发展速度就会落后。它另一个相当恶心的设计是，游戏里的农作物会枯萎。你种了庄稼，其机制是花一定量的钱买种子，种下去，过一阵子回来收割，就能赚到更多的钱。

cues.en: It's a very simple loop. But the crop withers after a certain amount of time if you don't come harvest it. So that suddenly makes you very worried to come check in at the game like, oh, I was going to play tonight, but I'm running late in traffic. So I'm going to whip out my iPhone and play Farmville on there so I can get my crops so they don't wither. These things are designed to make you worry about the game even when you're not playing the game. So cow clicker.
cues.zh: 这是一个非常简单的循环。但如果你没按时来收割，庄稼在一定时间后就会枯萎。这一下子就让你特别担心，心心念念着上线看一眼，比如“哎呀，我本来打算今晚玩的，但我路上堵车了，那我得掏出 iPhone 赶紧登上去收个菜，可不能让庄稼枯了”。这些设计的目的，就是让你就算没在玩游戏，心里也总挂念着它。接下来说说 Cow Clicker。

cues.en: So we've got a screen shot here. I only realized this today for some reason, but when I was talking about that strip down a game exercise, that's exactly what Cow Clicker is. It takes this genre of games and boils them down to the absolute essential. There's a cow, your cow that's in the middle of the screen, and you can click it. But instead of having a bunch of moves, you get one click. That's all you get. And then a six hour timer starts, and six hours later you get another click, right?
cues.zh: 这里有一张截图。不知道为什么，我今天才意识到这一点：我之前提到的“极简剥离游戏要素”的练习，Cow Clicker 正好就是这么做的。它把这类游戏提炼剥离，只保留最核心的本质。屏幕中央有一头奶牛，属于你的奶牛，你可以点击它。但你没有一堆行动步数，你只能点一次。就只能点一下。然后就会触发一个 6 小时的倒计时，6 个小时后，你才能再点一次，对吧？

cues.en: If you buy the in-game currency, which is Mooney, then you can spend that to get other clicks faster. So then you can click on your cow. And then if you invite friends into your pasture, you can all earn Mooney. So it's got all the same attempted virality that all of these games have. And of course, to amplify that virality, every once in a while, you click the cow, and it says, hey, you clicked your cow. Do you want to share the fact that you clicked your cow with your friends?
cues.zh: 如果你花钱买游戏里的代币，也就是 Mooney，就能花它来更快地获得点击次数。这样你就能点你的牛了。接着要是你邀请朋友来你的牧场，大家就都能赚 Mooney。所以它和其他游戏一样，全都是这种病毒式传播套路。当然了，为了放大这种传播效果，隔三差五你一点牛，它就会提示：嘿，你点了你的牛，想把这事分享给好友吗？

cues.en: And you do that, and then it goes into your friend feed like that. Hey, I'm clicking a cow. It's funny, but the reason that it's funny is because that's exactly what these games are. So you play Frontierville, and well, this is an email pestering, but it pastures you to sign up for emails. And then you're in there, and like, oh, I'm going to clean up my garden, so I'm going to clobber this fox that's keeping me from doing anything. And then it's like, oh, you clobbered a fox. Nice going. Do you want to share that with your friends?
cues.zh: 要是你真分享了，这消息就会直接出现在好友的动态流里。嘿，我正在点牛呢。这挺搞笑的，但之所以好笑，是因为这些游戏还真就是这副德行。比如你玩 Frontierville，好吧，这里有个邮件骚扰，它一直在烦你让你订阅邮件。然后你在游戏里想着，哦，我要打理一下花园，得先把这只碍手碍脚的狐狸揍跑。接着游戏就会提示：哇，你痛揍了一只狐狸，干得漂亮，想把这事分享给好友吗？

cues.en: And it does this all the time. If you haven't played this game, in the middle of those 14 moves, you probably get three nag screens like this, not an exaggeration. So you can barely even do what you're trying to do. So anyway, that alone would be dangerous enough. The fact that game designers have now maybe crossed some ethical line where they're explicitly designing games for you to be worried, explicitly designing them to decrease the quality of your life when you're not playing them.
cues.zh: 而且这种提示无时无刻不在弹。如果你没玩过这游戏，在这短短 14 次行动里，你大概能碰到三次这种弹窗骚扰，真的一点都不夸张。你甚至连自己想做的事都没法顺顺当当做完。总之，单是这样就已经够危险了。游戏设计师们现在可能已经越过了某种道德底线，他们就是在故意设计出让你焦虑的游戏，故意设计成在你没玩的时候，去降低你的生活质量。

cues.en: That's that's what they do oh, you know, okay, so I didn't finish making my point which is just that as Not good of a game design as I think World of Warcraft is it's at least made in Some way that's more innocent than that right like the guys who make World of Warcraft like Running around killing monsters with swords and stuff right and they envision some kind of audience that is like them Who would also like that kind of game?
cues.zh: 他们干的就是这种事。哦，对了，我刚才话还没说完，我的意思是，就算我觉得《魔兽世界》（World of Warcraft）的游戏设计不怎么样，但至少它的出发点还要单纯得多，对吧？做《魔兽世界》的那帮人，自己就喜欢提着剑到处跑、打打怪之类的，对吧？他们设想的受众也是和他们一样的玩家，同样会喜欢这类型的游戏。

cues.en: And even though it's a giant endeavor that's at some point no longer about pure joy when you're toiling to make a game, that's kind of what they're doing. They're making games for people who kind of like the same kind of thing that they do. I don't want to single out Farmville and Frontierville, but at any of the companies who make these games in a high-stakes kind of way, nobody there thinks this is a good game. They're not trying to make games for people to enjoy. They're simply trying to maximize.
cues.zh: 虽然制作一款游戏是项庞大的工程，辛勤劳作到一定阶段时，往往已经不再是纯粹的快乐了，但他们大体上还是在做这件事。他们是在为跟自己志趣相投的人做游戏。我不是专门要针对 Farmville 和 Frontierville，但在那些把这种商业模式做到极致的公司里，根本没人觉得这算是什么好游戏。他们压根没打算做出让玩家享受的游戏，他们只是在拼命最大化两个指标。

cues.en: Either the amount of money they get in from a user or the amount of virality they get from that user to contact other users or both. That's all they care about. And that's obvious by looking at the game design. If they wanted Frontierville to be more fun, there's a bunch of things they could do. They could give you more moves. They could even move to a system where your number of moves isn't limited. So you can just kind of tend your farm however you want. But that would make it less addictive. And their goal isn't enjoyability. It's addictiveness.
cues.zh: 要么从用户身上榨出最多的钱，要么通过这个用户拉来最多新用户的病毒式传播量，或者两者都要。他们关心的就只有这些。看看游戏设计就知道得很清楚了。如果他们真想让 Frontierville 更有趣，有的是办法。他们完全可以给你更多行动力，甚至可以干脆改成不限行动步数，让你随心所欲地打理农场。但那样一来，游戏的成瘾性就没那么强了。他们的目标从来不是好玩，而是让人上瘾。

cues.en: They could nag you less. This screen pops up right in the middle of whatever you're doing. You're going to run over and grab a piece of pie. And it's like, hey, share this with your friends. They could stop nagging you while you're in the middle of something and save the window for later. But they know that if they do that, you're less in the moment and are less likely to respond or to assent to this kind of virality. So that would be evil enough. But we have new technology.
cues.zh: 他们完全可以少烦你一点。你手头正忙着呢，这弹窗就啪地跳出来。你正要去拿块派吃，它就跳出来说：嘿，快分享给你的好友吧。他们完全可以在你忙的时候别来烦你，把弹窗留到后面再显示。但他们清楚，真要那样做，你当时那股兴奋劲儿一过，就不太可能去配合或响应这种病毒式传播了。这就已经够缺德了，但我们现在还有新技术，

cues.en: that makes it even easier. In the old days, making video games was like, you worked for a while on something, and you finish it, and then you deliver it to somebody's door. And you're like, here's my video game. Do you like it? And a lot of times they say no, but hopefully you sell enough of them. Now it's not like that, because now we have games on the internet. And games on the internet do this thing called A-B split testing to maximize profit. Web guys love this. Who knows what this is in the audience?
cues.zh: 让这种套路变得变本加厉。过去做电子游戏是这样的：你埋头开发一段时间，做完后把它打包送到玩家家门口。你说：“这是我做的游戏，你喜欢吗？”很多时候他们会说不喜欢，但只要卖出去的份数够多就行。现在可不是这样了，因为有了网络游戏。网游为了把利润榨到最大，会搞一种叫 A/B 测试的操作。做网站的那帮人最爱这套了。现场有谁知道这是什么吗？

cues.en: OK, small percentage, so I'll explain it. This is basically another kind of hill climbing algorithm, where instead of delivering one product to everybody, you split your audience into, let's say, two random samples, completely random.
cues.zh: 行，知道的人不多，那我解释一下。这本质上就是另一种爬山算法：你不再是给所有人提供同一款产品，而是把受众分成两个随机样本，完全随机的样本。

cues.en: You give half of them version A of the game and half of them version B of the game, right? Just like any scientist running a control in an experiment and then an experimental group. And what kind of things might you change between version A and version B? Well, maybe it's like the background color, right? To see how that affects people's psychology. Maybe it's a style of the main character to see what kinds of characters people identify with. Maybe it's like, you know, how much gold do I get for punching a fox?
cues.zh: 你给其中一半人玩游戏的 A 版本，另一半人玩 B 版本，对吧？就像科学家做实验设对照组和实验组一样。那 A、B 两个版本之间会改动什么呢？也许是改改背景颜色，对吧，看看这会对玩家的心理产生什么影响。也许是换换主角的风格，看看大家对哪种角色更有认同感。又或者，比如打一拳狐狸能拿到多少金币？

cues.en: And maybe it even varies by region. Maybe Americans like the game more if you get this much gold for punching a fox, but Europeans like it more if they get this much gold for punching a fox. And actually, I just like it more, but that's not even what they measure. What they measure is how many new players get attached to the system and how much new money they get from you buying micro-payment kind of things. That's what they're measuring with this A-B testing. And so what you do...
cues.zh: 甚至不同地区的数据都不一样。也许美国人更吃“打一拳狐狸给这么多金币”这一套，而欧洲人则更喜欢“给那么多金币”。其实我刚才说的是“更喜欢”，但他们测的根本不是喜不喜欢。他们真正测量的是：有多少新玩家沉迷进了这个体系，以及你们在微交易这类小额付费上又掏了多少钱。这才是他们用 A/B 测试去衡量的东西。所以做法就是……

cues.en: As you put out two versions, you see which one works better, and you throw the other one away, and then you start again. You put out two more versions and two more versions, and you keep going down this infinitely branching tree, and you're constantly optimizing your game all the time. Now, A-B testing by itself is not that new of a thing.
cues.zh: 你放出两个版本，看哪个效果更好，把不行的扔掉，然后周而复始。你再放出两个版本，接着又是两个版本，沿着这棵无限分叉的树一直往下走，时时刻刻都在优化你的游戏。当然，A/B 测试本身倒算不上什么新鲜玩意儿。

cues.en: If you work for a candy company in the 80s and you wanted to make a new candy bar, that's kind of an expensive endeavor to ship that out to everybody in the USA. So what you do is you maybe make two versions of the candy bar, and you put them in test markets. One of them is like Burlington, Vermont, and the other one is like Fresno, California or something. And you see how those do in various markets. And then if one of them is successful enough, you start selling that nationally. You scale it up. That takes a long time to do.
cues.zh: 如果你在80年代在一家糖果公司工作，想推出一款新糖果棒，把它铺到全美各地是件很烧钱的事。所以你可能做两个版本的糖果棒，投放到测试市场。一个像佛蒙特州伯灵顿，另一个像加州弗雷斯诺之类的。看看它们在各个市场表现如何。然后如果其中一个足够成功，你就开始全国销售。把它规模化。这要花很长时间。

cues.en: Compared to today, when you have web stuff, any company who has the user base, the size of one of these very popular games, like FarmVille or whatever, can run a very meaningful A-B test in a day, or in six hours, or even in one hour. So the iteration time isn't actually bounded by the time it takes to actually run the test now. It's more bounded by infrastructure issues at the company, like how quickly can they put the test together to make sure they're not breaking everybody's thing.
cues.zh: 相比之下，今天有 Web 这些东西，任何拥有像《FarmVille》之类热门游戏那样用户规模的公司，都能在一天、六小时甚至一小时内跑一次很有意义的 A/B 测试。所以现在迭代时间其实不受跑测试所需时间的限制，更多受公司基础设施问题的限制，比如他们多快能把测试搭起来，同时确保不会把所有人的东西搞坏。

cues.en: How quickly can they decide even what they want to test? So remember back before that I was saying we used to design games just by doing what we thought was cool. Imagine that's a weapon like a bow and arrow or something. And then we got a little more scientific about it. And we decided to watch people in a more empirical and observant way without trying to influence them. And imagine that's a weapon like a flintlock rifle. What you've got now on the web is something like this.
cues.zh: 他们甚至多快能决定自己想测试什么？还记得之前我说过，我们过去设计游戏，就是做自己觉得酷的东西。想象那是一种武器，像弓箭之类的。后来我们变得更有科学一点，决定以更经验性、更观察性的方式去看人，而不试图影响他们。想象那是像燧发步枪一样的武器。而你现在在 Web 上拥有的东西，差不多是这样。

cues.en: where it's just firing all the time. And that, at some point, the difference between this and this is not just a difference in quantity of projectiles. At some point, a quantitative difference becomes qualitative. At some point, you can just do totally different things with this new weapon than you could have done with the old weapon. And what kind of things can you do? Well, maybe...
cues.zh: 它一直在开火。而到了某个时候，这个和这个之间的区别就不只是弹丸数量上的区别了。到了某个时候，量变会变成质变。到了某个时候，用这种新武器，你能做的事和用旧武器能做的事完全不同。那你能做什么样的事呢？嗯，也许……

cues.en: You're not firing actual bullets, but you're doing psychological, experiment-y things and profiting off them. So there's another interesting thing that I think that's interesting about game design, is that game design is kind of a game by itself. I've made a bunch of puzzle games, and I've found that looking at a situation and saying, how do I make an interesting puzzle out of this is itself a really interesting puzzle. So there's this huge irony going on.
cues.zh: 你并不是在发射真正的子弹，而是在做心理上的、实验性的东西，并从中获利。所以我觉得游戏设计还有另一个有趣之处：游戏设计本身就像一场游戏。我做过一堆解谜游戏，我发现，看着一个情境然后想“我怎么把它变成一个有趣的谜题”，这本身就是一个非常有趣的谜题。所以这里有一种巨大的讽刺。

cues.en: that the companies that are making these social games that basically have no gameplay value in them, right, are actually themselves playing a much more interesting game than the game that they're making for you to play, right? The game they're playing is this huge multi-dimensional optimization problem where you're like trying to gather data and make the best decision and all that, and the game they're making for you to play is like clicking on a cow a bunch of times and you get some gold, right? So that's...
cues.zh: 那些在做这些社交游戏、而游戏里基本没什么玩法价值的公司，其实自己正在玩一场比他们做给你玩的游戏有趣得多的游戏，对吧？他们玩的游戏，是一个巨大的多维优化问题，你要收集数据、做出最佳决策之类的；而他们做给你玩的游戏，就是反复点一头牛，然后得到一些金币，对吧？所以那……

cues.en: you know, very strangely humorous. And as I visualize that happening, right, somebody at one of these companies, they're doing their A-B testing, they're kind of tweaking something for Europe and tweaking something for America and tweaking something for Canada, and then going over here and like, oh, this A-B test is done, let's look at the graphs of the results and let's write a report on that and stuff.
cues.zh: 挺奇特幽默的。我在脑海中勾勒出那个画面：在那些公司里，有人在做A/B测试，为欧洲市场调调这个，为美国市场改改那个，再为加拿大调整一下，然后转头说：“噢，这个A/B测试做完了，来看看结果图表，写份报告吧”之类的。

cues.en: It's a little bit like planting trees and rearranging a garden and minding livestock and all that. So you could say that the people making Farmville are not only playing a game, but they're playing some kind of like er Farmville that is way more interesting. And so the sad fact of what this all comes to is you've got these people. Farmville has a wide demographic. It's not just computer nerds who play it apparently anymore. So you've got all these people who think that they're playing this cool game.
cues.zh: 这有点像是在植树、修整花园、照料牲畜。所以你可以说，制作Farmville的人不仅在玩游戏，而且还在玩某种更高维的、更有趣的Farmville。而这一切带来的可悲事实是，你看看这些人——Farmville的用户画像非常广泛，显然不再只是电脑极客在玩了。所以有这么多人，自以为在玩一款很酷的游戏。

cues.en: You know, where they mind their cows and their pigs and they're feeling like the boss and they're getting all this gold and they're getting richer and their farm is looking nicer. There's all these ways that they feel like they're progressing, but what's actually happening is that someone is farming them, right? So, you know, there's all these imaginary farms out there where you gain imaginary money, but then there's a real farm with real money that pulls, you know, it pulls money from you over the internet. And you don't ever see it because that's all, like, behind your head while you're, like, typing into the computer.
cues.zh: 在游戏里，他们照看自己的牛和猪，感觉自己像个农场大亨，赚得盆满钵满，金币源源不断，农场也越变越漂亮。他们通过各种方式感到自己在不断升级，但实际情况是，有人正在“收割”他们，对吧？你看，虽然有这么多虚拟农场让你赚虚拟货币，但背后却存在着一个赚真金白银的真实农场，通过互联网把你的钱掏走。而你完全察觉不到，因为当你敲击键盘时，这一切都在你脑后悄然发生。

cues.en: So now I put all this up. The weapon analogy is a little heavy handed, but I honestly couldn't come up with anything better in the time available, which was like one day. But I actually don't think, like looking at this situation this way, like somebody is farming the players of Farmville, I don't think that this is hyperbole. I don't think it's any kind of distortion of reality. This is what is actually happening.
cues.zh: 所以我把这些都摆出来了。“武器”这个比喻可能有点过了，但老实说，在短短一天的时间里，我也想不出更好的比喻了。不过我觉得，从“有人在收割Farmville玩家”这个角度来看待这件事，其实并不算夸大其词。我绝不认为这是对现实的歪曲，这就是正在发生的事实。

cues.en: in San Jose or wherever their office is now, right now. Are they in San Francisco? All over the Bay Area it's happening. There's tons of these companies. Anyway, so you talk to game designers about anything. I mean, any time that I question current paradigms in game design, because I go to a lot of game conferences and talk to these people, game designers have a defense which is just like, look, man, we're just giving people what they want. They want to play our game. They're having fun, right?
cues.zh: 此时此刻，在圣何塞，或者不管他们的办公室现在搬到了哪里——是在旧金山吗？整个湾区都在发生这种事。这类公司多得数不胜数。话说回来，当你和游戏设计师聊起这些时，我的意思是，每当我质疑当前的游戏设计范式时——因为我常去参加游戏大会，经常和这些人交流——游戏设计师总有一套辩解套路，就像是：“听着，兄弟，我们只是给玩家他们想要的。他们想玩我们的游戏，他们乐在其中，不是吗？”

cues.en: That is true. I cannot exactly argue with that. People report that they're having fun, and certainly they pay money to play the game. But the fact is that, as we know from other areas of life, sometimes people want things that are not good, either not good for them or not good for people around them. Sometimes it's not good in a mild way, and sometimes it's not good in an extreme way, like they're ODing on heroin, and they're barfing all over the floor all the time.
cues.zh: 确实如此。这一点我确实无从反驳。玩家确实反馈他们玩得很开心，而且他们也确实花钱玩游戏了。但事实是，正如我们在生活其他领域所知道的那样，人们有时想要的东西并不好，要么对自己没好处，要么对周围的人没好处。有时这种“不好”比较轻微，而有时则极其严重，就像吸食海洛因过量，整天吐得满地都是那样。

cues.en: As a game designer, you can make your own decision about whether you care that what they want is not good for them, or about whether you want to exploit their susceptibility device and profit from it. My personal gut feeling is that all this FarmVille stuff is just evil. It's not even mildly evil. It's like if you go and look at the discussions that happen day to day at those companies among the designers, they are very evil. They are about stuff like, how do we get people thinking about our game?
cues.zh: 作为游戏设计师，你可以自己决定：究竟是在意他们想要的东西对他们没好处，还是想利用他们的软肋来大赚一笔。我个人的直觉是，像《FarmVille》这类东西简直就是纯粹的恶。甚至都算不上是轻微的恶。如果你去看看那些公司里设计师们平时的讨论，就会发现他们有多邪恶。他们讨论的都是这类问题：我们怎么才能让玩家一直念着我们的游戏？

cues.en: all day every day, right? How do we get them to buy the maximum number of things that have the minimum amount of utility for them in their real life? Because if they get a lot of utility out of it, you know, they get satiated, right? It's like, it's like, this is totally off the cuff, right? But it's like Coca-Cola, right? Coca-Cola and soft drinks like that get marketed as refreshing, but the ingredients in them actually do not refresh you in any way. They actually make your body a little bit thirstier, right? So that you'll want to drink more. That's how soft drinks work.
cues.zh: 整天都想着它，对吧？我们怎么才能让他们买最多的东西，但这些东西在现实生活中的用处又最小？因为如果真对他们很有用，他们就会感到满足，对吧？这就好比——我随口打个比方啊，就像可口可乐对吧？可口可乐这类软饮宣传说是提神解渴，但里面的成分实际上根本起不到解渴的作用。它们反而会让你身体更渴一点，对吧？这样你就会想喝更多。软饮就是这么运作的。

cues.en: And FarmVille and all those games are like that. Another thing designers say is, hey man, it's just games. It's just an entertaining pastime. Don't get so serious about it. But I have to take this very seriously, because quantity matters, and video games are becoming very, very popular. Going back to drinks, if you drink some alcohol once in a while, it's cool. It's totally fine. It's a nice beverage that gets you a little tipsy.
cues.zh: 而《FarmVille》和所有这类游戏也是一个套路。设计师们常说的另一套话是：哎呀，就是个游戏嘛。不过是消遣娱乐而已，别那么上纲上线的。但我必须非常严肃地看待这件事，因为量变引起质变，而且电子游戏正变得越来越流行。再拿饮料来打比方，如果你偶尔喝点酒，挺好的，完全没毛病。喝点好酒，让人微醺一下。

cues.en: If you get stinking drunk like four or five days a week, then you're going to be seeing that doctor that we talked about earlier, because your liver is going to be dead. Everybody knows that. That's not controversial. Quantity matters in that case. In a similar way, if one person wastes a little bit of time with some stupid game that doesn't do anything for them, that's no big deal. But when you have a nation of people who spend a large amount of time on something that's not just a waste of time, but that actively
cues.zh: 但如果你一周有四五天都喝得烂醉，那你就得去看我们前面提到的那个医生了，因为你的肝脏快完蛋了。大家都懂这个道理，这毫无争议。在这种情况下，摄入量很关键。同理，如果某个人玩了个毫无收获的蠢游戏浪费了点时间，那也没什么大不了的。但如果全国有大量的人花大把时间在一件不仅是浪费时间，而且还在主动……

cues.en: kind of makes them a little dumber, poorer, sheep-like, and infantilized. That becomes a much more serious issue. And as huge and popular as video games are right now, they're only going to get more popular. I don't see them declining anytime soon. And so I think as game designers, we have a responsibility. And I'm speaking of me and my friends and anyone in the audience who thinks they might be a game designer someday.
cues.zh: 让他们变得更迟钝、更贫穷、更像顺从的羊群、更幼稚化的事情上。这就成了极其严重的问题。而且电子游戏现在已经如此庞大和流行，未来只会变得更加普及。我看不出它近期有任何衰退的迹象。因此我认为作为游戏设计师，我们肩负着一份责任。我指的是我和我的朋友们，以及台下所有认为自己未来可能会成为游戏设计师的人。

cues.en: We have a responsibility proportional to the number of people that we will affect with our products. And I want to talk about something closely related, because I feel like people are a little bit dead into this kind of issue, because we face it in simpler and more obvious to see ways all the time, like psychological manipulation. You go out to buy things, and everything is priced in something that ends in $0.99 or $0.95. Why is that? It's because if you sell something for $9.99,
cues.zh: 我们所承担的责任，与我们的产品将影响到的人数是成正比的。我还想聊聊一件紧密相关的事，因为我觉得大家对这种问题有点麻木了，毕竟我们在日常中总能以更简单、更明显的方式遇到它，比如心理操纵。你出门买东西，所有东西的定价都是以 99 美分或 95 美分结尾。为什么会这样？因为如果你把东西定价为 9.99 美元，

cues.en: You make way more money than if you sell it for $10 because more people will buy it because obviously $9.99 is a lot cheaper than $10, right? Well, no, I mean obviously it's not as thinking intelligent rational creatures, right? We know this is stupid. This is kind of insulting because I know I know what $10 is right? I know what $9.99 is. There's just not really a difference but Despite the fact that we believe that on an intellectual level This gets to us
cues.zh: 你赚的钱会远比卖 10 美元多得多，因为买的人会更多，毕竟显然 9.99 美元比 10 美元便宜多了，对吧？额，不是的，我是说作为有思考能力、聪明且理性的生物，显然并非如此对吧？我们知道这很蠢，甚至觉得有点被侮辱智商，因为我知道 10 美元是多少对吧？我也知道 9.99 美元是多少。其实真没什么区别，但尽管我们在理性层面上明白这一点，它依然会暗中

cues.en: at a lower level. It affects at least enough people to make this the only real strategy for selling something. But beyond that, it affects people who think that they're immune to it. Like, oh, I'm a smart guy. Advertising doesn't work on me. Everybody thinks that kind of thing. But it's not true. So another example from the field of video games, Microsoft points, which you buy things with on the Xbox 360.
cues.zh: 在潜意识层面影响我们。它至少影响了足够多的人，以至于这成了唯一的行销策略。不仅如此，它甚至能影响那些自以为能免疫的人。比如觉得，“噢，我是个聪明人，广告对我没用。”每个人都会这么想。但事实并非如此。再举一个电子游戏领域的例子：微软点数（Microsoft Points），也就是你在 Xbox 360 上买东西用的点数。

cues.en: are intentionally, you know, they're engineered so that the conversion ratio between Microsoft points and US dollars is like, is it...
cues.zh: 都是故意设计的，它们被精心算计好，让 Microsoft 点数和美元的兑换比例变成……是多少来着？

cues.en: $800 to $10? Yeah, that's what it is. It's something that doesn't evenly divide, so that you can't easily do the math in your head about how much something really costs. If you're really used to the system, you might know that an 800-point gain costs $10, but something like $1,200, it takes you a little longer to think about how much that is, so you don't really think about it as much, or at least that's the hope. This is intentional. $9.99 is intentional. And the problem is that we walk around every day with these insults in our face. $9.99 says, I'm going to manipulate.
cues.zh: 800 点换 10 美元？对，就是这样。它根本除不尽，这样你就很难在脑子里心算出它到底值多少钱。如果你非常熟悉这个体系，可能知道 800 点的游戏值 10 美元，但要是换成 1200 点这种数字，你就得多琢磨一会儿它到底是多少钱，这样你就不会去细想了，至少他们是这么指望的。这都是故意的。9.99 美元也是故意的。问题在于，我们每天都在顶着这些侮辱性的套路过日子。9.99 美元的意思就是：“我要操纵你。”

cues.en: to manipulate you at the level of human responses that you don't have control over, I'm not going to treat you as an intelligent human being because I know I'll make more money off you that way, right? That's what these things are. Now, of course, if you want to buy my last game, Raid, you can buy it for $9.99 on Steam or 800 Microsoft points.
cues.zh: “我要利用你无法控制的本能反应来操纵你，我不会把你当成一个有智慧的人对待，因为我知道这么做能从你身上赚到更多钱”，对吧？这些套路就是这个意思。当然，如果你想买我的上一款游戏《Braid》，你可以在 Steam 上花 9.99 美元买，或者花 800 Microsoft 点数。

cues.en: I'm at least complicit in this. I don't exactly have control over setting pricing on any of these channels, but by participating in that, I support it. And there's this thing where, as a game designer, you just have to pick your battles. You can't fight every fight all the time.
cues.zh: 我至少也是这套把戏的帮凶。我其实无法控制这些渠道的定价，但只要参与其中，我就是在支持它。作为一名游戏设计师，你必须有所取舍。你不可能在每一场战斗中都去抗争。

cues.en: So the best I could do with something like Braid is to try and make a wall and insulate it so that outside the game, all this kind of horrible stuff happens. And inside the game is kind of a garden where I respect the player and I treat them as an intelligent person who I would like to know and talk to.
