And unfortunately, I wasn't even able to do that because of achievements, but I cut that from the talk. So if you want me to rant about achievements, ask me a question later.
cues.zh: 所以在做《Braid》这类游戏时，我所能做到的极限，就是尽量筑起一道墙将它隔绝开，让墙外去发生各种糟糕透顶的事情。而游戏内部则像是一座花园，在这里我尊重玩家，把他们当作我想结识、想交流的聪明人来对待。遗憾的是，由于成就系统的存在，我甚至都没能完全做到这一点，不过我把这部分内容从演讲里删掉了。如果你们想听我吐槽成就系统，待会儿提问环节可以问我。

cues.en: But, you know, I wanted to bring this thing up and the fact that I engaged in it to make a very clear point that my goal in this talk isn't to convince you, you know, not to treat people like machines or resources and that FarmVille is evil because it farms people, because it treats them like resources. That's not exactly it. Because we're biological creatures and certainly like all of biology, all of the history of evolution has been about creatures treating other creatures as resources, right? That's what biologists learn when they come to college.
cues.zh: 但是，我想提这件事以及我也身处其中的事实，是为了明确表达一个观点：我今天演讲的目的，并不是为了劝大家不要把人当成机器或资源，也不是要说《FarmVille》很邪恶，因为它在“收割”玩家、把人当资源看待。不完全是这样。因为我们是生物，而在整个生物界、整部进化史中，生物一直都在把其他生物当作资源，对吧？这就是生物系学生上大学时学到的东西。

cues.en: if they didn't know it already. When you have some hamburger for dinner, you're treating a cow as a resource. And dealing with people is often not any different, though hopefully not food-wise. So my goal among all this storm of conflicting ideas is to try to respect the player and avoid manipulating them.
cues.zh: 如果他们之前还不知道的话。当你晚餐吃汉堡时，你就是把牛当成了资源。与人打交道往往也没什么两样，虽然希望不是指吃人这方面。所以，在这一大堆相互冲突的观念中，我的目标是尽量尊重玩家，避免去操纵他们。

cues.en: Because manipulation is not a sign of respect. Not only am I going to treat you like a resource, but I'm going to do it in such a way that I don't really care that you're mistreated, and I'm going to profit off it. The problem that I have is that these good game design things that I talked about, the best practices at the beginning of this talk, are all, to one degree or another, in either subtle ways or obvious ways, manipulative tactics.
cues.zh: 因为操纵算不上尊重。这不仅意味着我把你当作一种资源，而且是以一种哪怕你被苛待我也毫不在意的方式，我还要从中牟利。我所担忧的问题在于，我前面提到的那些优秀的游戏设计理念，也就是本演讲开篇所说的那些最佳实践，无论程度深浅，无论隐蔽还是明显，全都是操纵性的手段。

cues.en: And that's why abstract games like chess or Go don't have them, because there's like nobody there. There's not enough content in those games to actively manipulate you. But video game designers actively manipulate their players all the time. And I have a problem with this, because I don't want to manipulate my players. But if I'm going to be a competent game designer, if I'm going to make games that people want to play,
cues.zh: 这就是为什么像国际象棋或围棋这类抽象棋类游戏没有这些，因为里面根本没有人性的投射。那些游戏里没有足够的内容来主动操纵你。但是电子游戏设计师却时时刻刻都在主动操纵玩家。我对此心存芥蒂，因为我不想操纵我的玩家。但如果我想成为一名合格的游戏设计师，如果我想做出大家想玩的游戏，

cues.en: that are video games. And they probably have to incorporate some of these items. So just like pricing something at $9.99 if I want to actually have enough money to make my next game, I probably have to use at least some of these practices if I'm going to make a game that enough people want to play that I'm allowed to make my next game. And so trying to design a good game according to good game design practices today while respecting the player is a very difficult thing to do.
cues.zh: 做出电子游戏。那么它们大概率就必须融入其中的某些手法。所以这就好比把价格定在 9.99 美元一样，如果我真想赚够做下一款游戏的钱，想做出一款有足够多的人想玩、让我有机会继续做下一款的游戏，我就大概率至少得用上其中的一些做法。因此，如今想要按照优秀的游戏设计规范来设计一款好游戏，同时又要尊重玩家，是一件非常困难的事。

cues.en: Earlier in the talk, I described boredom as having an evolutionary purpose and frustration having an evolutionary purpose. Well, fun probably also has an evolutionary purpose. And so what is that purpose? And is the fun you're having with a particular game fulfilling that purpose, or is it not? And if it's not fulfilling that purpose, what does that mean in terms of the fitness function in evolution or whatever you want to think about? And the second thing to ask is,
cues.zh: 在之前的演讲中，我说过无聊具有进化上的目的，挫败感也具有进化上的目的。那么，“好玩”大概也有进化上的目的。那个目的是什么？你从某款游戏中获得的乐趣，到底有没有实现那个目的？如果没有实现，从进化中的适应度函数或者你所能想到的任何角度来看，这又意味着什么？第二个要问的是：

cues.en: You say you're having fun, but is it really fun? I used to play a lot of Counter-Strike. I used to be ranked in Counter-Strike and in a very serious clan and stuff. And I really would play that game a whole lot. It was a very interesting game. I'm glad I spent a lot of time playing it. It absolutely was not fun. Very serious, very hardcore game. But most people will report if you ask them if it's a fun game. Oh yeah, Counter-Strike's really fun. But look up some synonyms for fun.
cues.zh: 你说你玩得很开心，但这真的算“好玩”吗？我以前经常玩 Counter-Strike。我曾在 Counter-Strike 里有排名，还在很厉害的战队里等等。我那时确实玩得非常多。那是一款非常有趣的游戏，我很庆幸自己花了很多时间去玩。但它绝对谈不上“好玩”。它是一款非常严肃、非常硬核的游戏。但如果你问大多数人，他们都会回答：“啊对，Counter-Strike 很好玩。”但你去查查“好玩”的同义词吧。

cues.en: You find words like joyous or things like that. When you're playing one of these hardcore first person shooters, ask yourself a different synonym of fun. Is this a joyous experience that I'm having? You'll find very quickly that it isn't. And so what we see is that the word fun is being used as a linguistic catch-all for a number of other different things that are very complicated.
cues.zh: 你会看到像“愉悦”之类的词。当你在玩硬核第一人称射击游戏时，试着用“好玩”的其他同义词问问自己。我现在体验到的是“愉悦”吗？你很快就会发现并不是。所以我们看到，“好玩”这个词只是被当作一个语言学上的箩筐，装下了许多非常复杂的其他东西。

cues.en: Right? And so starting to introspect into that, into what exactly is this fun that I'm having, what's the nature of it, and how does it affect my life is sort of the road to understanding these things better. And the rest of the answer to this is what I'm not going to answer. I'm going to let Alan Moore answer it. This is from a documentary called The Mindscape of Alan Moore. And he says, writers and people who had command of words were respected and feared as people who manipulated magic.
cues.zh: 对吧？因此，开始反思这一点，反思我体验到的这种“好玩”到底是什么、它的本质是什么、它如何影响我的生活，正是更好地理解这些问题的途径。而这个问题的其余部分，我不会亲自回答。我要让 Alan Moore 来回答。这段话出自纪录片《The Mindscape of Alan Moore》。他说：作家和驾驭文字的人曾经受人敬畏，被视为操纵魔法的人。

cues.en: In latter times, I think that artists and writers have allowed themselves to be sold down the river. They have accepted the prevailing belief that art and writing are merely forms of entertainment. They're not seen as transformative forces that can change a human being, that can change society. They're seen as simple entertainment, things with which we can fill 20 minutes, half an hour, while we're waiting to die. It is not the job of artists to give the audience what the audience want.
cues.zh: 在近代，我认为艺术家和作家听任自己被出卖了。他们接受了主流观念，认为艺术和写作仅仅是娱乐形式。它们不再被看作能够改变一个人、改变社会的变革力量。它们被视为单纯的消遣，是在等待死亡的过程中，用来打发二三十分钟时间的东西。艺术家的职责并不是给观众他们想要的东西。

cues.en: If the audience knew what they needed, then they wouldn't be the audience. They would be the artists. It is the job of the artist to give the audience what they need. Thanks for your time. Thank you for listening. And I will take questions if anyone wants to say after. OK, so we have microphones. If you'd like to ask a question, make sure you wave your hands vigorously in the air, and we'll get a microphone to you. There's a guy up there waving his hands.
cues.zh: 如果观众知道自己需要什么，他们就不会是观众了。他们就会是艺术家。艺术家的职责是给观众他们需要的东西。谢谢大家的时间。感谢大家的聆听。如果有人想留下来，我可以回答几个问题。好的，我们有麦克风。如果大家想提问，请一定要使劲挥手，我们会把麦克风递给你。上面有位朋友在挥手。

cues.en: Anyway. OK. Well, sorry for preempting you, Guy, up there. But you mentioned that you felt compelled to engage in these manipulative practices in order to be successful. And compelled is not the right word, but yeah. It's something I'd better pay attention to, to be a competent game designer in the modern age, now that we're not making 80s style games anymore. Right. Yeah. And I'm wondering, if I view that in terms of art,
cues.zh: 不管怎样。好的。抱歉先抢了上面那位朋友的提问。不过您之前提到，您觉得为了取得成功，不得不采用这些操纵性的做法。用“不得不”不太准确，但确实如此。要想在现代成为一名合格的游戏设计师，既然我们不再做 80 年代风格的游戏了，这确实是我最好要关注的事。是的。没错。我很好奇，如果从艺术的角度来看待这一点，

cues.en: can hear similar things from artists I know saying that they have to work to make their art accessible. And if you view this in terms of products that you're designing for people, maybe this is affordability and ease of use. And where is the line between making something accessible and affordable and easy to use and making something that is manipulative, which is perhaps similar, but... No, it is absolutely a little bit similar, but...
cues.zh: 我也听过我认识的艺术家说过类似的话，他们说必须努力让自己的艺术平易近人。如果从面向大众设计产品的角度来看，这也许就是易得性和易用性。那么，让东西变得平易近人、易得、易用，与让东西具有操纵性，这两者之间的界限在哪里？它们也许很相似，但是……不，它们确实有一点相似，但是……

cues.en: It's something that you have to answer for yourself while you're making something, I think. I'm not going to say to anybody, here's the line where this is manipulative, but this is merely helpful. That's part of what having a strong opinion about what you're making is. And that's part of where the work comes from when you're doing it. I definitely, when I'm making something, have strong feelings about whether something is too far in that direction.
cues.zh: 我觉得，这是你在创作过程中必须自己回答的问题。我不会对任何人说，这条线是操控，那条线只是有帮助。这正是对自己做的东西有强烈立场的一部分。也是你做这件事时，工作动力的一部分。我在创作时，确实会强烈感觉到某样东西是不是在那个方向上走得太远了。

cues.en: And I absolutely cut things back. There's sort of a tutorial in Braid, but it's wordless. And you walk in and it just puts icons for the buttons on the screen. And that assumes a certain level of video game literacy, if you're playing the game. But I was OK with that, because it's a video game literate kind of game. And I didn't want to handhold people. First of all, because it would spoil the mood. Excessive handholding is not really what the game is about.
cues.zh: 我绝对会做删减。Braid 里算是有一个教程，但它是无字的。你走进去，它只是在屏幕上放出按键图标。这假设了玩家有一定程度的电子游戏素养。但我觉得可以，因为这就是一款面向有游戏素养玩家的游戏。我不想手把手带人。首先，那会破坏氛围。过度手把手引导并不是这个游戏的核心。

cues.en: But also because of that respect thing, because Braid was about, you know, so there's two things that are active, right? There's my opinion as a designer, and then there's like what the game is about. And both of those colluded agreed on the same decision. Because Braid is about discovering stuff. It's about the game sitting back, and you have to figure it out, and you have to come to the conclusions. It's not going to tell you. So an overbearing tutorial actually would not fit that theme. But I think that
cues.zh: 但也因为那个尊重的问题，因为 Braid 讲的是，你知道，这里有两个东西在起作用，对吧？一个是我作为设计师的看法，另一个是游戏本身要表达的东西。这两者合谋达成了一致的决定。因为 Braid 讲的是发现。它讲的是游戏退后一步，你得自己弄明白，你得自己得出结论。它不会告诉你。所以一个强势的教程其实不符合这个主题。但我觉得，

cues.en: Even something like an overly, like a lot of Japanese games have tutorials, modern Japanese games, have tutorials that are very, very hand-holdy, where you have to click through tons and tons of text, and I don't feel respected by those at all. I feel like they think I'm six years old, and I would never make that kind of thing. But there's a middle ground that's totally reasonable. So you mentioned earlier that we humans have evolved, and I think the game designers have evolved, as you pointed out, to adapt to what generates more money.
cues.zh: 甚至像那种过度——比如很多日本游戏、现代日本游戏都有教程，非常非常手把手，你得点过成吨成吨的文字，我完全不觉得被尊重。我觉得他们把我当成六岁小孩，我绝不会做那种东西。但有一个完全合理的中间地带。你之前提到人类进化了，而我认为，正如你指出的，游戏设计师也进化了，去适应更能赚钱的东西。

cues.en: So if you follow this line of thought to the logical conclusion is that the conclusion is that people like you will be dang specious because you would not be making enough money so people would not be adapting your style. So that concerns me because that means in the future we'll be getting more and more games like Farm View. I don't actually think that's exactly the conclusion. I mean I agree with you that that's a concern.
cues.zh: 所以如果你顺着这个思路推到逻辑结论，结论就是：像你这样的人会变成濒危物种，因为你赚不到足够的钱，所以人们不会去效仿你的风格。这让我担心，因为这意味着未来我们会看到越来越多像 Farm View 这样的游戏。其实我不认为结论完全是这样。我的意思是，我同意你所说，这是一个值得担心的问题。

cues.en: But to go back to evolution, I don't want to beat the evolution thing into the ground because it's not meant as a precise metaphor here, and you can use evolution to explain anything you want, including things that are clearly wrong. But in ecosystems, things find niches that are quite profitable for them.
cues.zh: 但回到进化，我不想把进化这件事说烂，因为这里并不是要把它当作精确的比喻，而且你可以用进化解释任何你想解释的东西，包括明显错误的东西。但在生态系统里，事物会找到对自己相当有利的生态位。

cues.en: They're able to live nice lives and whatever. And they're not dominating the ecosystem, but they don't have to. I already don't dominate the ecosystem. A game made by Electronic Arts that's very successful will sell probably 20 times what a game that I make will sell. But I don't need to be Electronic Arts, because they have this giant elephant body, and I have a tiny ant body. So I think it's OK. It's OK to not try to maximize, because you don't need everybody to buy your game.
cues.zh: 它们能过上好日子之类的。它们没有主导整个生态，但也不必如此。我本来也没主导生态。Electronic Arts 做的一款非常成功的游戏，销量大概是我做的游戏的 20 倍。但我不需要成为 Electronic Arts，因为他们有巨大的大象身躯，而我只有小小的蚂蚁身躯。所以我觉得这没问题。不追求最大化也没关系，因为你不需要所有人都来买你的游戏。

cues.en: You don't need some nebulous like demographic the size of the United States or of the world to all like what you make. You only need a small number of people to like what you make very much enough that they'll go out of their way to hear about it and get it and play it. And that's how it worked for my last game and I hope that that continues to be viable in the future. Certainly the internet makes that much more viable now than it was any time in the past because in the past distribution was tightly controlled through retail stores and it was very hard to get into a retail store.
cues.zh: 你不需要某个模糊的、像美国或全世界那么大的用户群体都喜欢你做的东西。你只需要一小部分人非常喜欢你做的东西，喜欢到愿意特意去了解它、获取它、玩它。我上一款游戏就是这么成的，我希望未来这条路仍然可行。当然，互联网让这件事现在比过去任何时候都更可行，因为过去发行被零售店牢牢控制，想进入零售店非常难。

cues.en: Now that's not true. So if you have people who are interested enough in what you're doing, they can get what you're doing. They can get your thing, your product. Who was first? I have it right here. What you talked about a lot was single player challenge games. I'm right here. Like where you're playing against a machine or people that you don't see. How do you, where do you see social games fitting into your perspective or your one dimensional line? Okay. So I don't exactly like the name social game because
cues.zh: 现在情况不是这样了。所以，如果你有一群对你做的东西足够感兴趣的人，他们就能拿到你做的东西。他们能拿到你的东西、你的产品。谁先来？我这儿就有。你讲了很多单人挑战类游戏。我就在这儿。比如你对抗机器，或者对抗你看不见的人。你怎么看社交游戏放进你的视角，或者你那条一维路线里？好。其实我不太喜欢“社交游戏”这个名字，因为

cues.en: The games that are social, like on Facebook and stuff right now, are not actually very social. Like you don't interact with people, right? It's a very passive thing. So I'm assuming that you mean not games that have social elements, but that exact genre of game. I'm talking about games like the Wii structured games where they're trying to get people together and use... So like same room multiplayer kind of thing. Yeah. And what do I think about that? Well, because...
cues.zh: 现在像 Facebook 上那样的社交游戏，其实并没有那么社交。你并不会和人互动，对吧？它非常被动。所以我猜你说的不是那些带有社交元素的游戏，而是那个特定类型。我说的是像 Wii 上那种结构化游戏，它们试图把人聚在一起，用……就是同房间多人游戏那种。对。那我怎么看这个？嗯，因为……

cues.en: They're used more as a social tool to get people together and do things. So it seems like it's a different direction than single player challenge games. Sure, it definitely is. The games that I talked about today, a lot of them are single player, but I would more say that they tend to be games with a very heavy design hand.
cues.zh: 它们更多是被当作社交工具，用来把人聚到一起做点什么。所以这看起来和单人挑战类游戏是不同方向。当然，绝对是。我今天讲的游戏，很多是单人游戏，但我更想说，它们往往是有很强设计主导的游戏。

cues.en: And one reason that there's a lot of single player stuff there is because single player games have a lot of content. Because that's what you do is you chew through the content. And something like Wii Sports, you're playing tennis a bunch of times or whatever. And it's not the same content heavy experience. And so the designers don't necessarily do this big giant infrastructure of manipulative work in those games. That said, I find Nintendo's aesthetic for that kind of game kind of schmaltzy. And it is a little bit manipulative and insulting, I think.
cues.zh: 而其中有很多单人内容的一个原因，是单人游戏有很多内容。因为你做的就是不断啃内容。而像 Wii Sports 这种，你只是反复打网球之类的。它不是同样内容密集的体验。所以设计师不一定会在那些游戏里做庞大的一整套操控性工作。话虽如此，我觉得 Nintendo 那类游戏的美学有点煽情。而且我认为它有点操控性，甚至有点侮辱人。

cues.en: But not nearly in the same way as something like Farbville. Totally, totally different magnitude of things. But as for those games, yeah, it's a totally cool direction to go in game design. There's lots of different ways to go, and I certainly can't talk about them all. I have two questions about Braid. Sure. Well, the game starts with a background of a village burning down. So what's going on?
cues.zh: 但远不像 Farbville 那种方式。完全是不同量级的东西。不过说到那些游戏，是啊，在游戏设计里那是个非常酷的方向。可以走的路有很多，我当然没法全都讲到。关于 Braid 我有两个问题。好。游戏开场背景是一个村庄在燃烧。那到底是怎么回事？

cues.en: I think that if you are playing the game, and you're standing there, and you're watching that opening screen, then you see exactly what's going on in the opening screen. Well, I finished the game already. Yeah, so you know. Don't spoil it. I mean, I'm not even trying to not spoil it. I'm just saying that that's like the reason, OK, the reason that I make video games.
cues.zh: 我觉得如果你在玩这个游戏，站在那里看开场画面，那你看到的就是开场画面里正在发生的事。呃，我已经通关了。对，所以你知道。别剧透。我的意思是，我根本没在刻意不剧透。我只是说，那差不多就是原因，好吧，是我做电子游戏的原因。

cues.en: Like I used to when I was early in college, I wrote a little bit of science fiction and got some stuff published. It's under a pseudonym, so you can't look it up. Did I know you back then when I was writing that stuff? You probably didn't see it. The reason that I make games is because at some point, I found myself wanting to get at ideas that are pretty grand, and they don't lend themselves very well to linguistic explanations.
cues.zh: 就像我大学早期那会儿，我写过一点科幻小说，还发表了一些东西。是用笔名发表的，所以你查不到。我写那些东西的时候认识你吗？你大概没看过。我做游戏的原因是，某个时候我发现自己想触及一些相当宏大的想法，而它们不太适合用语言来解释。

cues.en: Because language is very serializing. And if you want to get at something that's extremely multidimensional and extremely nebulous and yet extremely important to people, if you're doing it through this process where you have to unserialize all this language and then somehow rebuild it into this thing, it's a very difficult and error-prone process. It doesn't exactly work. Video games, like film, for example, is different because it gives you this higher bandwidth experience. And you can do stuff visually.
cues.zh: 因为语言非常序列化。如果你想触及某种极度多维、极度模糊、却又对人们极其重要的东西，如果你要通过这个过程来做：你必须先把所有这些语言反序列化，然后再设法把它重建为那个东西，那会是一个非常困难且容易出错的过程。它并不完全奏效。电子游戏，比如电影，就不一样，因为它给你这种更高带宽的体验。而且你可以用视觉的方式来做东西。

cues.en: in ways that you can't exactly do in other media. And video games, because they have interactivity, they allow you to explore a space. And because they allow you to explore the space, because they allow a player to explore the space, they allow the designer to communicate the shape of that space more implicitly than you can with language, because it is found as opposed to told. And that's important.
cues.zh: 以其他媒介无法完全做到的方式。而电子游戏因为具有交互性，允许你探索一个空间。又因为它们允许你探索空间，允许玩家探索空间，它们让设计师能比用语言更隐式地传达那个空间的形状，因为那是被发现的，而不是被讲述的。这很重要。

cues.en: part of why the medium is respectable as its own thing. And it's not just like film with interactivity or whatever. So when I do something like that, that opening scene, which that first level in grade, if you load up the level editor and you see how many objects are there, it's way more complicated than any other level in the game. And it's just to do these certain effects and have the camera pan in a certain way and all this stuff.
cues.zh: 这也是为什么这种媒介本身值得尊重的一部分原因。它不只是带交互的电影之类。所以当我做那样的东西时，那个开场场景，也就是 Braid 的第一关，如果你打开关卡编辑器，看看那里有多少对象，它比游戏里其他任何关卡都复杂得多。而这一切只是为了做出某些效果，让镜头以特定方式平移，诸如此类。

cues.en: And it's because we cared a lot about what was happening there. But as far as I'm concerned, the entirety of the communication of what is happening there is contained in the game. And that's all that needs to happen. And that's why I make video games. So that's why I don't want to tell you. What was the other question? Too many questions. Something that's becoming more prevalent with online distribution is downloadable content. Do you feel that it's just another way?
cues.zh: 这是因为我们非常在乎那里发生的一切。但在我看来，关于那里发生的一切，我想传达的内容都已经包含在游戏里了。这就足够了。这也是我做电子游戏的原因。所以我才不想直接告诉你。另一个问题是什么来着？问题太多了。随着网络发行的普及，DLC也越来越常见。你觉得这只是一种手段吗？

cues.en: for companies to make more money by offering additional content to players? Or is it a way for companies who weren't quite able to get the content created during development a way to get extra stuff out there for the players to enjoy? It's not B. And the reason why is because it takes a long time to download or to develop and debug downloadable content.
cues.zh: 是公司通过向玩家提供额外内容来赚更多钱？还是说，这让那些在开发期间没能把内容做完的公司，能有机会把额外内容做出来给玩家体验？不是后者。原因在于，开发和调试可下载内容需要耗费大量时间。

cues.en: Studies have shown that the optimum window to release your DLC, there's been a few studies and they conflict a little bit, but they all have the same general conclusion, which is that the optimal time to release your DLC is right when the game releases, because that's when the most people are paying attention to your game. Games are a very hit-driven thing, where it's like movies, where everybody wants to go see the new movie, and then they're not interested. Even if it's a good movie, they probably won't watch it if it's like five years old, right?
cues.zh: 研究表明，发布DLC的最佳窗口期——虽然有几项研究彼此稍有出入，但大体结论是一致的——也就是发布DLC的最佳时间，正是游戏发售的那一刻，因为那时关注你游戏的人最多。游戏是一个极度依赖爆款的行业，就像电影一样，大家都想去看新片，过后就没兴趣了。即使是一部好电影，如果已经是五年前的了，大家大概率也不会去看了，对吧？

cues.zh: 不满于用语言去探索宏大的思想，因为语言本质上是线性的。他对于小说的线性特质感到有些沮丧，觉得它根本无法反映自己每天从成千上万条离散数据中构建现实的方式，也无法反映无聊的本质及其价值，以及文学中许多后现代的

cues.en: tricks in literature really serve to either entertain the reader without doing a whole lot or serve the darker purpose of telling the reader, look how smart and author I am. cues.zh: 花招，究竟只是为了纯粹取悦读者，还是带着某种更阴暗的目的向读者炫耀：“看我这个作家多聪明”。诸如此类的还有很多。是的，我完全不觉得意外。当然，正因为他是个作家，他才试图去尝试截然不同的东西。但我总觉得，如果你擅长自己所处的媒介，你就能看清它的局限性，对吧？
